description: This knowledge graph models activities as the primary domain entities, with each activity described by an identifier, a human-readable activity name, and an assigned type/classification. Typical queries filter or retrieve activities by their identifier, name, or type.

Knowledge graph of participation records linking students with activities; main entities are participation events (records), students, and activities. Each participation record includes attributes such as activity identifier, student identifier, references to the activity and student, and a type/class annotation.

This knowledge graph models faculty participation in activities, representing faculty members, activities (events or projects), and the participation relationships that connect them. Key attributes include faculty identifiers, activity identifiers, reference identifiers linking to external records, and type metadata for each participation record.

This knowledge graph describes university or college faculty members as the primary entities. Each faculty member is characterized by attributes commonly used for lookup or filtering—such as faculty ID, first and last name, phone number, academic rank, office building and room, and sex.
This knowledge graph describes university student records. It contains student entities with attributes such as student ID, first and last name, age, sex, major, advisor, and city (city code).

A knowledge graph of competitive flight events (matches/races) that represents events, pilots and aircraft along with places and dates. Each event records attributes such as country, date, location, round, fastest qualifying result, winning pilot and winning aircraft (and references to those winners).

This knowledge graph describes airports and their operational/traffic statistics. Each airport entity includes identifiers and name, aircraft movements, passenger counts (domestic, international, transit, total), freight in metric tonnes, and percentage change metrics (e.g., year-over-year).

A knowledge graph about associations between airports and aircraft, representing records that link specific aircraft to specific airports. Key entities are aircraft, airports, and the linking records, with important attributes including aircraft identifier, airport identifier, record identifier, and reference fields that point to the aircraft and airport.

This knowledge graph describes pilots as the primary domain, representing individual pilot entities. Each pilot is characterized by key attributes such as name, age, a pilot identifier, and its class/type membership.

This knowledge graph describes aircraft and related aircraft entries as the primary entities. Each aircraft record includes key attributes such as an aircraft identifier, descriptive text, maximum disk loading, total disk area, maximum gross weight, and other aircraft-specific properties.

A knowledge graph of university student records describing individual students as the primary entities. Each student is characterized by attributes commonly used in queries such as advisor, age, city code (location), first name, last name, major, sex, and student identifier.

This knowledge graph describes allergy records linking people (typically students) to their known allergies. Each allergy record connects a student identifier to an allergy description and includes attributes for the allergy itself plus reference identifiers for the allergy and the student.

This knowledge graph models allergy-related information centered on allergy-type entities. Each allergy-type entity records the specific allergy (e.g., the allergen or allergy name) and an attribute describing its allergy type or classification.

Knowledge graph of apartment reservations, describing bookings of rental units by guests. Each booking record includes identifiers for the booking, apartment, and guest, along with booking start and end dates and a booking status code.

A knowledge graph about apartment buildings and residential properties, where the primary entities are individual buildings. For each building it records key attributes useful for filtering or selection such as building ID, full and short names, street address, textual description, building manager, and contact phone number.

This knowledge graph describes the availability and status of units (e.g., apartments) and their associated bookings. Key entities are unit status records linking units and bookings, with important attributes including booking ID, unit/apartment ID, availability flag (yes/no), reference booking/unit IDs, and the status date.

This knowledge graph describes residential apartment units and their relationships to buildings. Each apartment entity is characterized by attributes such as a unique identifier, unit/apt number, apartment type code, counts of bathrooms, bedrooms and rooms, and a reference to its building.

This knowledge graph describes apartment facility records, representing associations between apartments and the facilities available to them. Main entities are apartment-facility entries and apartments, with key attributes including apartment identifier, facility code (the specific facility), reference apartment identifier, and the entity type.

This knowledge graph contains records about guests (individual persons) in a hospitality/customer-management context. Key entities are individual guests and their primary attributes include a unique guest identifier, first and last names, date of birth, and gender code for identification and filtering.

This knowledge graph describes bridges, with each entity representing an individual bridge. Key attributes include unique identifiers, name, architect identifier and its reference, location, and length measurements in feet and meters — properties commonly used to filter or select bridge records.

This knowledge graph describes mills and related mill records, representing individual mill entities. For each mill it provides key attributes useful for querying or filtering such as unique identifier, name, location, built year, architect (and architect reference), type, and descriptive notes.

A knowledge graph about architects, representing individual architect entities with key attributes including unique identifier, name, gender, nationality, and type/classification. It is suitable for retrieving or filtering architect records by those attributes.

This knowledge graph describes third-party companies (e.g., vendors or suppliers) and their organizational records. Key entities are company records with attributes such as company identifier, company name, company address, company type, and other company details.

This knowledge graph describes maintenance engineers, representing individual engineer records and their affiliations to companies. Key attributes include engineer identifiers, company identifiers (and company references), first and last names, and other descriptive details.

This knowledge graph models associations between engineers and the skills they possess, with primary entities representing engineer-skill association records that link individual engineers to specific skills. Key attributes include engineer identifiers, skill identifiers, and reference identifiers that relate or reference the engineer and skill entities, along with type metadata for each record.

A knowledge graph describing skills and competencies for workforce or domain expertise analysis. Its primary entities are individual skill records, each annotated with attributes such as skill_id, skill_code, skill_description, and an associated type/classification.

This knowledge graph catalogs faults associated with physical parts (part failures and their relationships). Each fault record includes key attributes such as a unique part-fault identifier, the associated part identifier (and any referenced part IDs), a short fault name, and a detailed fault description.

This knowledge graph describes relationships between assets and their constituent parts, modeling records that link an asset to a part and to referenced assets or parts. Key entities are asset-part association records, with primary attributes including asset identifier, part identifier, referenced asset identifier, referenced part identifier, and a record type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes maintenance contracts and their associated companies. Each contract record includes attributes such as contract ID, company ID (and company reference), contract start date, and contract end date.

This knowledge graph describes fault log records for assets in an operational/maintenance domain, capturing individual fault log entries linked to specific assets and reporting staff. Key attributes include asset identifiers, fault descriptions, fault log entry IDs and timestamps, and the IDs of the staff who recorded the entries (including references to related asset and staff records).

This knowledge graph describes organizational physical assets and related records, including individual assets, supplier companies, and maintenance contracts. Key attributes include asset identifiers, make and model, acquisition and disposal dates, descriptive details, supplier references, and maintenance contract references.

A knowledge graph describing staff members of an organization, with each staff entity characterized by attributes such as staff name, staff ID, gender, and other staff-related details. Typical queries target or filter staff records by name, identifier, gender, or additional descriptive fields.

This KG describes records of parts associated with fault logs in equipment or systems, modeling fault-log-part entries and their links to specific part faults and fault log entries. Each entry includes identifiers for the fault log entry and the part fault, a fault status, and reference links to related fault log entries or part faults.

This knowledge graph models field engineer visits for service fault handling, representing entities such as engineer visits, engineers, contact staff, and fault log entries; key attributes include visit identifiers, engineer identifiers, contact-staff identifiers, associated fault-log identifiers, fault status, and visit start/end datetimes.

This knowledge graph describes which skills are required to fix equipment or part faults, with main entities being part-fault records, skill records, and the associations that link faults to required skills. Key attributes include identifiers and reference identifiers for parts/faults and for skills that associate a given fault or part with the skills needed to repair it, plus type metadata for each association.

A knowledge graph describing parts/components in an inventory or product catalog. Each part entity includes identifiers and names, a classification/type label, and billing-related attributes such as a chargeable flag (yes/no) and a chargeable amount.

This knowledge graph describes colleges and higher-education institutions as the primary entities. Each college is represented with key attributes including a unique college identifier, the institution's full official name, and geographic location details (city, state, country).

This knowledge graph contains records about baseball players, capturing biographical and career information. Each player entity includes attributes such as given and family names, multiple player identifiers (e.g., internal id, reference ids), birth and death dates and locations, physical attributes (height, weight), batting and throwing handedness, and career dates like debut and final game.

A knowledge graph of parks and park entities. Each park is described by attributes such as a unique identifier, official name and aliases, classification/type, and location details (city, state, country).

A knowledge graph of professional baseball historical and seasonal data, representing players, teams and franchises, managers, games (regular and postseason), awards, and Hall of Fame records. Key attributes include season/year and entity identifiers plus performance and roster metrics such as games, at-bats, hits, home runs, RBIs, batting averages, pitching stats (ERA, wins, losses, strikeouts, saves, innings), fielding stats (errors, assists, positions), team-level metrics (wins, attendance, standings), salaries, award votes, and postseason outcomes.

A knowledge graph about ships and naval vessels, representing individual ship entities and their characteristics. Key attributes include identifiers and names, ship type and tonnage, current or historical location, disposition/status (e.g., lost in battle) and references documenting battle losses.

This knowledge graph contains records of death/casualty incidents, primarily linking fatalities and injuries to ships that caused them. Each record represents a death event and includes an identifier, counts of killed and injured, descriptive notes, and references to the causing ship.

Knowledge graph of historical battles, modeling individual battle events as entities. Each battle is described by attributes such as name, date, identifier, outcome/result, and commanding figures (notably Bulgarian and Latin commanders).

A knowledge graph of people and individual person profiles. Key attributes available for each person include name, birth date, birth place, physical measurements such as height and weight, and a unique person identifier (people_id), which are commonly used for filtering or selection.

This knowledge graph represents athletes (body builders/weightlifters) and their performance records. Key entities are individual athletes and linked people records, with important attributes including athlete identifiers and lift results such as snatch, clean and jerk, and total.

This knowledge graph contains bibliographic records of publications (primarily books), with publications as the main entities. Each record includes key attributes such as book and publication identifiers, price, publication date, publisher, and references to related books.

This knowledge graph describes books and their associated metadata. Key entities are individual books, with attributes such as a book identifier, title, writer (author), issue information (e.g., edition or issue number), and classification/type.

This knowledge graph describes web client accelerator instances and related client devices/software, modeling individual accelerator/client entities and their network connections. Key attributes include client identity and identifier, connection details or status, human-readable name, and operating system.

This knowledge graph describes compatibility relationships between accelerators and web browsers. Each compatibility record links an accelerator and a browser (with accelerator and browser identifiers and reference identifiers) and includes attributes such as the year since they became compatible.

This knowledge graph describes web browser products/brands; its main entities are individual browsers or browser variants. Key attributes for each browser include an identifier, its name, market share, and type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes people (individual persons) and their personal and physical information. Each person is represented with attributes such as a unique identifier (people_id), name, date of birth, sex, height, and weight.

This knowledge graph contains political candidate polling records, representing candidates and associated people identifiers. Each record includes identifiers for the candidate and related person(s), the poll date and source, and quantitative polling metrics such as support, oppose, consider and unsure rates.

This knowledge graph contains automotive data about individual cars/vehicles as the primary entities. Key attributes include performance and engine specifications such as acceleration, horsepower, number of cylinders, engine displacement, fuel efficiency (mpg), vehicle weight, model year, and record identifiers.

This knowledge graph covers automotive nomenclature, representing car name entries (vehicle models and related records). Each entry includes attributes such as manufacturer (make), manufacturer identifier (make id), model name, reference model, and a type/classification attribute.

A catalog of product or device models and their manufacturers. Each model entity is described by attributes such as maker (manufacturer), model name, model identifier, a reference to the maker, and its semantic type/class.

Knowledge graph of countries where the main entities are individual countries described by attributes such as country identifier, country name, continent (and links to continent records), and type/classification information. These attributes are the primary fields users would filter or select when querying the dataset.

A knowledge graph of automobile manufacturers and related entities. For each car maker it records attributes such as a unique identifier, full name and maker/brand designation, country of origin, and links/references to country entities.

A geography-focused knowledge graph about world continents, representing individual continent entities. Each continent record includes attributes such as a unique continent identifier, the continent name (label), and type/classification metadata.

This knowledge graph describes cinemas (movie theaters) and related information. Each cinema entity is characterized by attributes such as a unique identifier, name, location, seating capacity, and opening year.

This knowledge graph describes cinema screening schedules, representing showings of films at specific cinemas. Each schedule entry links a film and a cinema and records attributes such as cinema ID and film ID, screening date, show times per day, ticket price, and references to the corresponding cinema and film.

A knowledge graph of films and serialized screen entries, representing individual film or episode entities and their metadata. Each entity is described by attributes such as title, director, a unique film identifier, production code, original air date, number-in-season (episode/season position), and rank within a series.

This knowledge graph contains monthly temperature records for cities, where each entity represents a city's temperature measurements. Key attributes include monthly temperature values for January through December and identifiers linking the record to a city and to a reference city.

Knowledge graph about cities, primarily representing city entities (including Chinese cities with names in Hanzi and Hanyu Pinyin). Key attributes include the city name, city identifier, GDP, and regional population.

This knowledge graph describes which cities hosted specific matches or events, linking match records to their host cities. Key entities are match records and hosting-city records (cities), with important attributes including match identifiers, host city identifiers or names, the hosting year, and reference links to the match and city records.
This knowledge graph contains records of sports matches. Each match entity is described by attributes such as competition, date, unique match identifier, result, score, and venue.
This knowledge graph covers mountains, representing mountain entities with key attributes such as name, unique identifier, height, prominence, country, and mountain range.

This knowledge graph describes mountain climbers and their ascents. It contains entities for individual climbers and linked mountains, with attributes such as climber identifier, name, country, mountain identifier(s) (and reference mountain id), points scored and time of the ascent.

This knowledge graph represents academic student records; the primary entities are students, each described by attributes such as advisor, age, city code (location), first and last name, major, sex, and a student identifier.

This knowledge graph contains information about clubs (organizational or recreational entities). Each club entity includes attributes such as name, identifier, location, and a textual description, along with class/type metadata.

Knowledge graph describing student club membership records, linking students to clubs. Key entities are membership records, students and clubs, with important attributes including student ID, club ID, the member's position/role, and reference identifiers that link to the student and club records.

This knowledge graph describes retail shops as entities, capturing key attributes for each shop such as address, number of staff, opening year, quality score (rating), and a unique shop identifier. It is suitable for queries that filter or aggregate shops by location, size, age, or rating.

A knowledge graph of a customer/loyalty membership system describing individual members and their characteristics. Key entities are members, with attributes such as name, member ID, address, age, membership card, level of membership, and time of purchase.

This knowledge graph describes happy hour promotions and events associated with retail or foodservice shops. Key entities are happy hour records and shops, with attributes such as a happy hour identifier, month, number of staff in charge, shop identifier, and reference shop identifier.

This KG describes happy-hour membership records for a promotional/loyalty program, where each entity represents a member’s participation or account. Key attributes include the happy-hour/program ID, the member ID and reference member ID, and the total amount associated with the member (e.g., spent or credited).

This knowledge graph models university professors and their employment/organizational information. Each professor entity includes attributes such as department affiliation (department code and department reference), employee number (and its reference), office location, phone/extension, and highest academic degree.

This knowledge graph describes organizational departments (for example university or institutional departments), with each entity representing a department. Key attributes include department name, department code, address, phone/extension, associated school code, and employee-related fields such as employee number and reference employee number.

This knowledge graph describes university or college courses as the primary entities. For each course it records key attributes such as course code, credit value, textual description, associated department code, and any referenced department code.

This knowledge graph describes university class offerings and scheduling information. It represents class entities (course sections) with attributes such as class code and course code, section number, meeting time, classroom, instructor identifier, and references to related courses or instructors.

This knowledge graph describes employee records in an organizational HR domain. Key entities are individual employees with attributes used for identification and employment management, such as employee number, first name, last name and initial, date of birth, hire date, and job code.

A knowledge graph of course enrollments at an educational institution, modeling enrollment records that link students and classes. Each enrollment record includes attributes such as student number, class code (and references to the student and class entities) and the enrollment grade.

A knowledge graph of student records at an educational institution, describing individual students and their academic affiliations. Key attributes include student identifiers and names (including initials), date of birth, class level, GPA and credit hours, department and professor associations, contact phone, and transfer status.

This knowledge graph models student course enrollment records, describing instances of students taking courses. Each enrollment record includes attributes such as student ID, course ID, section ID, semester, year, grade, and links referencing the related student and course.

This knowledge graph describes university students and their academic details. Each student entity includes attributes such as student identifier, full name, department affiliation (department name and a reference to the department), and total earned credits.

This knowledge graph models advisors in an academic/advising domain as the primary entities. Each advisor record contains identifier and cross-reference attributes used for lookups and joins, such as an internal identifier, a referenced internal identifier, a referenced student identifier, and a student identifier.

This knowledge graph describes university course sections (individual class offerings) and their relationships to courses and locations. Key attributes include course identifier and section identifier, semester and year, time slot, building and room number, and links referencing the related course and building records.

This knowledge graph models academic teaching assignments or course offerings, representing individual "teaches" records for courses in an educational context. Key entities are teaching records linking courses and sections to a specific semester and year, with important attributes including course identifiers, section identifiers, semester, year, record IDs, and references to related course or record identifiers.

This knowledge graph models university/college courses as the primary entities, representing an academic course catalog. Each course is described by attributes such as course identifier, title, credit value, department offering the course, and a referenced department name.

Knowledge graph describing instructors at an educational institution. It represents instructor entities with attributes such as unique identifier, personal name, department affiliation (department name and department reference), and salary.

This knowledge graph describes classroom spaces in an educational or campus context. Each classroom entity is characterized by attributes such as building location, room number, seating capacity, and room type.

A knowledge graph about academic course prerequisite relationships. It contains records representing prerequisite links between courses and their prerequisite courses, with key attributes including course identifiers, prerequisite identifiers, referenced course identifiers, and referenced prerequisite identifiers used for selection and filtering.

This KG models scheduling/time-slot information for events or appointments. Its primary entities are individual time-slot records, each identified by an ID and described by temporal attributes such as day, start hour and minute, and end hour and minute.

This knowledge graph describes organizational departments (e.g., university or institutional departments) as the primary entities. For each department it records key attributes such as department name, budget, building/location, and type/classification.

This knowledge graph models student enrollments in courses, representing enrollment records that connect students and courses. Each enrollment record includes key attributes such as student identifier, course identifier, grade, and reference links to the student, course, and grade entities.

This knowledge graph describes membership and appointment records linking members to organizational units (e.g., departments and faculties) within an institutional or academic domain. Key entities are member/appointment records and organizational units, with important attributes including appointment type, department identifier, faculty identifier, and reference identifiers for department and faculty.

This dataset describes academic courses and their associated information. Each course record includes identifiers and metadata such as course ID, course name, credit value, meeting days and hours, department number, assigned instructor, and links to the referenced department and instructor.

This knowledge graph describes student records in an academic context, with the primary entities being individual students. Each student is characterized by attributes such as student ID, first and last name, age, sex, major, advisor, and city code.

This KG describes organizational departments (e.g., university or company departments), with entities representing individual departments. Key attributes available for filtering or selection include department name, department number, division, building and room location, and phone contact.

A knowledge graph of university faculty members describing individual faculty as entities and their identifying and contact details; key attributes include faculty ID, first and last name, phone number, academic rank, office building and room, and sex.

This knowledge graph represents student minor enrollments, modeling records that link students to academic minors or departments. Key entities are the minor-enrollment records, students, and departments/programs, with important attributes including student identifiers, department/program numbers, and reference links to the student and department records.

This knowledge graph models academic grade conversion information, with entities representing grade-conversion entries or records. Each entry links a letter grade to its corresponding numerical grade point and includes classification/type metadata for the conversion entry.

A knowledge graph about employees in an organization, representing individual staff members and their personal and employment-related information. Key attributes include first and last names, middle initial, social security number, birth date, sex, address, salary, department number, and supervisor identifier.

This knowledge graph catalogs dependents associated with employees. Each dependent is described by attributes such as name, birth date, sex, relationship to the employee, and the employee identifier (e.g., SSN) linking the dependent to their employee.

This knowledge graph describes employee work assignments linking employees to projects; each assignment record is an entity that relates an employee identifier to a project and records the number of hours worked. Key attributes include the employee identifier, the project number, and hours worked for each assignment.

A knowledge graph of organizational departments where the primary entities are department records. Key attributes include department name, department number, manager social security number, manager start date, and department classification/type, which can be used to identify, filter, or group departments.

This knowledge graph describes projects as the primary entities, with each project characterized by attributes such as project number, project name, department number, location, and its classification/type.

This knowledge graph describes organizational departments and their locations. It contains department entities with key attributes including department location, department number, and class/type membership for each department.

This knowledge graph describes companies, with entities representing individual firms annotated by company identifier and name, headquarters location and industry, and financial attributes such as assets, market value, profits, and sales (values recorded in billions).

This knowledge graph describes individual people and their demographic/educational information. Each person entity includes attributes such as name, age, nationality, graduation college, and a unique person identifier.

A knowledge graph of employment data describing records that connect people and companies. Each employment record identifies the person and the company (including reference identifiers linking to related entries) and includes attributes such as the year(s) worked.

This knowledge graph describes buildings and related built-environment information. It contains individual building entities with attributes useful for lookup and filtering such as identifier, name, city/location, height, number of stories, and development/status (e.g., completed or under construction).

A knowledge graph of companies, containing entities that represent individual firms and their identifiers and names. Key attributes include headquarters location, industry classification, and numeric financial metrics — assets, market value, profits, and sales (reported in billions).

This knowledge graph describes corporate office locations, representing office-location records that connect companies and buildings; key entities include offices, companies, and buildings, and important attributes include building identifier, company identifier, move-in year, and reference identifiers linking to the building and company.

This knowledge graph describes occurrences of singers performing in concerts, representing relationships between singer and concert entities. Each record links a singer to a concert and includes attributes such as concert identifier, singer identifier, and reference fields that point to the concert and the singer.

Knowledge graph about musical singers and their songs, representing individual singer entities and associated song records. Key attributes include singer name and unique identifier, age, country, gender, song name, and song release year.

This knowledge graph describes stadiums and related sports venues as the primary entities. For each stadium it records attributes such as name, capacity, location, and numeric metrics labeled average, highest, and lowest that can be used for filtering or selection.

This knowledge graph models concerts and their associated stadium/venue information; the primary entities are concert events (and linked stadiums). Important attributes used for queries include concert identifiers, concert names, stadium identifiers or references, event theme, and year.

This knowledge graph contains county-level public safety data, with each main entity representing a county or county public safety record and its associated police force. Key attributes include county identifier, name and location, population, number of police officers and police force, residents-per-officer ratio, crime rate, and case burden.

This knowledge graph describes cities (municipalities) and their identifiers and county relationships. For each city it provides key attributes such as the city name, city and county identifiers, and demographic breakdowns by race/ethnicity (American Indian, Asian, Black, Hispanic, Multiracial, White).

This knowledge graph describes teachers (educational personnel) as the primary entities, with key attributes including name, age, hometown, and a unique teacher identifier, and it also records each entity's type/class membership.

This knowledge graph describes educational courses as the primary domain, representing individual course instances. Each course is characterized by attributes such as its name/title, a unique course identifier, a starting date, and a type/classification, which are the main fields queries would select or filter by.

This knowledge graph describes course arrangement records in an educational context, where the primary entities are course-offering entries that link courses and instructors. Key attributes include course identifiers, teacher identifiers, reference course and teacher identifiers, and grade level, which are commonly used for filtering and selection.

This knowledge graph contains metadata about documents and their associated templates. Each document entity includes identifiers, a name, a textual description, and links to template identifiers (including reference template IDs) that relate documents to template records.

This knowledge graph describes metadata about organizational templates, capturing template records and their lifecycle. Key entities are template instances, with important attributes such as template ID, template details, template type code (and reference type code), effective-from and effective-to dates, and version number.

This knowledge graph represents paragraphs extracted from documents, where the primary entities are paragraph records characterized by their textual content. Key attributes include paragraph identifier, source document identifier, paragraph text, and referenced (cross-linked) document identifiers for tracing references between documents.

A knowledge graph of reference template types for a value management system, where each entity represents a specific template type. Each template type is characterized by a code identifier, a human-readable description, and a classification/type attribute that queries typically filter or select.

A knowledge graph of document drafts and their metadata, representing individual draft records. Each draft entity is characterized by attributes such as document identifier, draft number, draft details (content or metadata), references to related document IDs, and type/classification.

A knowledge graph of document records for trade and logistics processes, representing individual documents and their associated administrative and shipping information. Key attributes include document identifiers, document status and type codes (and their reference codes), shipping agent codes, receipt date and number, and other free-text details useful for filtering and selection.

A knowledge graph of reference document types for document classification and metadata management. Each document type entity includes a document-type code, a human-readable description, and a type/classification label.

A knowledge graph of shipping agents and their registry entries for logistics and maritime operations. Each entity represents a shipping agent and includes key attributes such as agent code, agent name, descriptive information, and type/classification.

This knowledge graph models circulation history of documents within an organization, representing circulation records that link documents, specific drafts and copies, and the employees involved. Each record includes attributes such as document identifier, draft number, copy number, employee identifier, and references to related document/draft/copy entries and referenced employees.

This knowledge graph models records of mailed documents, capturing mailing events and the associated entities such as documents and recipient addresses. Each record includes key attributes like document identifier, recipient address identifier, mailing date, and optional references to related document IDs and referenced recipient address IDs.

This knowledge graph contains metadata about draft copies of documents, representing each draft-copy entity and its relationships. Key attributes describe copy number, document identifier, draft number, and references to another document’s identifier and draft number.

A knowledge graph of address records describing physical or mailing addresses. Each address entity is characterized by an address identifier and detailed address information, and entries are grouped by their entity type.

This knowledge graph describes roles within an organization or value network, where the primary entities are individual role records. Each role is characterized by a role code (identifier), a textual role description, and a classification/type that can be used to filter or select roles.

A knowledge graph of organizational employees where the primary entities are individual employee records. Each employee is described by attributes such as employee ID, employee name, other details, role code, and references to role information.

A knowledge graph of reference document statuses used in a records/ document-management domain; its primary entities are document status records, each described by a status code, a human-readable status description, and an associated classification/type.

This knowledge graph models records of documents to be destroyed, treating each record as a document entity with identifiers and audit metadata. Key attributes include document ID, planned destruction date, actual destruction date, the employee who performed the destruction, and the employee who authorised the destruction (plus corresponding reference identifiers).

This knowledge graph models document location records, representing which documents were present at which locations over time. Key entities are documents and location-entry records, with important attributes including document identifier, location code, date-in-location (from and to), and associated reference dates.

A knowledge graph of organizational personnel, centered on individual employee entities; key attributes include employee identifier, employee name, date of birth, gender, and role codes (including referenced role codes).

This knowledge graph describes a collection of stored documents and their metadata. Each document record includes key attributes such as a document identifier, document name, document type code, date stored, and reference date stored.

A knowledge graph of organizational roles and functions. Each role entity is represented with key attributes such as role code, role name, and role description, plus type/class annotations for categorization.

This knowledge graph contains reference calendar entries representing individual calendar days and related date records. Each entry is described by attributes such as the calendar date value, the day number (position within a period), and a record type/classification.

This knowledge graph contains reference information about locations; its primary entities are location records (individual places or sites). Each location is described by key attributes such as a location code, a location name, a textual location description, and type/classification metadata.

A knowledge graph of reference document types, describing the different kinds of documents used in the system. Each entity represents a document type and includes key attributes such as document type code, name, description, and an associated type/classification.

This knowledge graph contains metadata about documents related to projects, representing document records and their associations with projects. Each document entity is described by attributes such as document identifier, name, date, document type code, project identifier, and reference type/project codes.

This knowledge graph describes financial account records, with accounts as the primary entities. Each account is characterized by attributes such as account identifier, account details, statement identifier, reference to statement IDs, and type annotations, which are the main fields used for filtering or selection.

Knowledge graph of reference document types: entities represent individual document type records and include key attributes such as a code, a human‑readable name, a textual description, and their classification/type.

This knowledge graph covers financial documents and expense records; its primary entities are documents (expense entries) and their linked references. Key attributes include document identifiers, descriptive document details, budget type codes, and references to related budget or document identifiers for linking and filtering.

This knowledge graph contains reference data for budget types used in financial and budgeting contexts; its main entities are budget type records that represent distinct budget categories. Each record is characterized by a budget type code, a human-readable budget type description, and type/classification metadata that can be used to filter or group entries.

This knowledge graph represents statements or claims as its primary domain. Each statement entity is described by a unique statement identifier, a referenced statement identifier linking to related statements, detailed statement content or metadata, and a type/classification.
This KG describes projects and their metadata. Each project entity includes key attributes such as a project identifier, descriptive project details, and a type/classification label.

This knowledge graph contains postal address records (locations) as its primary entities; each address includes an identifier and key attributes such as address line 1, address line 2, city/town, and state/county.

Knowledge graph describing customers and their contact/identification information. Each customer entity includes attributes such as customer ID, name, email address, phone number, address identifier (and reference to an address) and other miscellaneous details.

This KG describes customer orders and bookings in a retail/logistics context, modeling entities such as orders/bookings, customers, stores, and workshop groups. Key attributes include order/booking identifiers, customer and store identifiers (and reference links), order date, planned and actual delivery dates, and status codes.

A knowledge graph of clients/customers and their contact and identification data. Each client entity includes attributes such as client ID, customer name, email address, phone number, address identifiers (and references to address records), and other miscellaneous details.

This knowledge graph describes drama workshop groups or store locations and their associated contact and administrative information. Key attributes include workshop-group identifiers, store name, email address, phone number, address identifiers (and referenced address), currency code, marketing/region code, and other details.

This knowledge graph contains invoice records for commercial transactions, representing invoices and their associated orders, order items, and products. Key attributes include invoice identifiers, order identifiers and references, order item identifiers, product identifiers, order quantities, and payment method codes.

This knowledge graph describes service and product offerings, representing individual service records and associated products. Each service entity is characterized by attributes such as product name, product price, service identifier, service type codes, and workshop group identifiers (including reference codes) useful for filtering or selection.

Knowledge graph of performers associated with bookings/orders in an event or booking system. Each record links a performer to an order and includes attributes commonly used for filtering or selection, such as order identifier, performer identifier, reference order identifier, reference performer identifier, and entity type.

This knowledge graph describes performers (individuals or organizations) and their contact and identification details. Key entities are performer records, with important attributes including performer ID, associated address references, customer name, email address, phone number, and other descriptive details.

This knowledge graph describes booking service records, representing individual booking/service entries within an order/product domain. Each record includes attributes such as order identifier, product identifier, referenced order identifier, referenced product identifier, and the entity's type or classification.

A knowledge graph describing product items in a catalog/retail domain. Main entities are individual products, with key attributes including product identifier, product name, product price, and product type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes retail store locations and related organizational information. Its primary entities are stores, with key attributes including store identifier, store name, contact details (phone and email), address identifiers and reference addresses, marketing region codes, and other descriptive details.

A knowledge graph of reference service types for an information system, describing the catalogue of service-type entities. Each service-type entity is characterized by a service type code, a parent service type code (hierarchical relationship), a human-readable service type description, and a type/classification attribute.

This knowledge graph describes marketing regions used for geographic and market segmentation, with individual marketing region entities as the primary objects. Each region is characterized by attributes such as a region code, region name, a descriptive text, and type/classification metadata suitable for lookup or filtering.

This knowledge graph models order-item data in an e-commerce/order-management domain, where each entity represents an individual item within a customer order linking a product to an order. Key attributes include order identifier, order‑item identifier, product identifier, item quantity, and explicit references to the parent order and product.

This knowledge graph describes customer orders in a retail/commerce domain, representing order records and their associated customers and stores. Each order entity includes identifiers (order_id, customer_id, store_id and reference IDs) and temporal attributes such as order_date, planned_delivery_date, and actual_delivery_date.

Knowledge graph of invoice line items and their relationships to invoices, sales orders, order line items, and products. Each invoice-item entity records identifiers (invoice item ID, invoice ID, order ID, order-item ID, product ID), order quantity, other item details, and cross-references between invoices and orders.

This knowledge graph describes payment methods used in financial and transactional contexts; its main entities are individual payment method records. Each payment method is characterized by attributes such as a code identifier, a textual description, and a type/classification.

A knowledge graph of physical locations (places) where each location entity is described by key attributes such as a unique identifier, a human-readable name, an address, and its type/class. These attributes are the primary fields used to find, filter, or display location records.

This knowledge graph describes hotels and their attributes. It contains hotel records (unique identifiers) with key properties such as star rating codes (and referenced star rating), price range, whether pets are allowed, and type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes tourist visits to attractions, modeling individual visit records that connect tourists with tourist attractions. Each visit record includes attributes such as visit ID, tourist ID, attraction ID (and reference identifiers linking to those entities), visit date, and textual visit details.

A knowledge graph of tourist attractions where each entity represents an individual attraction, characterized by attributes such as name, location identifier, attraction type (and its reference code), unique attraction identifier, and practical information on how to get there.

This knowledge graph describes visitors/tourists and their records. Its primary entities are individual tourists, with key attributes including a unique tourist identifier, detailed tourist information (e.g., profile or visit details), and type/classification metadata for each visitor.

A reference dataset of attraction (tourism) types and categories used to classify points of interest. Each entity represents an attraction type and includes key attributes such as a code identifier, a textual description of the type, and its classification.

This knowledge graph describes photographic records of tourist attractions. Each photo entity includes metadata such as filename, title/name, a unique photo identifier, and links to tourist-attraction identifiers (including referenced attraction IDs).

This knowledge graph describes staff members associated with tourist attractions, representing individual staff entities and their links to attractions. Key attributes include staff identifiers, staff names, and the tourist-attraction identifiers or reference IDs that associate each staff member with a specific attraction.

This knowledge graph contains reference data about hotel star ratings, representing individual rating categories as entities. Each rating entity includes key attributes such as a star rating code and a textual description of the rating (along with its classification/type).

A knowledge graph of tourist attraction features, describing which specific features or amenities are associated with individual tourist attractions. Key entities are tourist attraction feature records and the tourist attractions they reference, with important attributes including feature identifiers, references to feature and attraction IDs, and type/classification metadata.

A knowledge graph of feature records describing characteristics or capabilities, where each feature is represented as an entity. Key attributes include a feature identifier, descriptive details (textual description), and a type/classification used to group or filter features.

Knowledge graph about theme parks, containing entities that represent individual parks. Each park entity includes properties such as a theme park identifier, a reference identifier, descriptive details, and classification/type information.

This knowledge graph represents retail shops as the primary entities, cataloging individual store instances. Each shop is described by identifiers (primary and reference shop IDs), descriptive details about the shop, and classification/type information used for filtering or selection.

This knowledge graph covers the domain of museums, representing individual museum entities and their records. Key attributes include descriptive museum details, unique museum identifiers and reference identifiers, and type/classification metadata that queries commonly filter or retrieve.

Knowledge graph about street markets, with entities representing individual markets; key attributes include descriptive market details, market identifiers (primary and reference IDs), and classification/type information.

This knowledge graph describes royal family entities and their class/type classifications. Key attributes are identifier fields (a primary royal-family ID and a reference ID) and type labels used to categorize each entity.

This knowledge graph describes institutional student enrollment records by campus, capturing enrollment statistics for academic years. Key entities are enrollment records (per campus and year) with attributes such as campus identifier/name, referenced campus, academic-year full-time-equivalent (FTE) counts, total enrollment for the academic year, and the year.

This dataset describes academic discipline enrollment records at university campuses, capturing how many students are enrolled in each discipline at different campuses and years. Key entities are enrollment records, disciplines and campuses, with important attributes including year, undergraduate and graduate student counts, and campus identifiers/references.

This knowledge graph models faculty-related records for an educational institution, representing individual faculty members and their organizational affiliations. Key attributes include campus location and reference-campus links, faculty identifiers/names or department information, and associated year and type classifications.

This knowledge graph describes campus fee records for CSU (California State University), with entities representing individual campus fee entries. Each entry includes key attributes such as the campus (name or identifier), the fee amount, a reference campus code, and the year, which are commonly used for filtering or selection.

This knowledge graph describes academic degree records and degree programs at educational institutions. Each degree entity includes attributes such as campus location, degree name or type, a reference campus identifier, the year awarded, and its classification/type.

This knowledge graph describes educational campuses, representing individual campus entities and their locations; each campus record includes key attributes such as campus name, county, geographic location, a unique identifier, and an associated year (e.g., establishment or record year).

A knowledge graph of cultural companies and their associated cultural entities, covering companies and linked book clubs and movies. Key attributes include company name, place of incorporation, group equity shareholding, entity type, and identifiers or cross-references for book clubs and movies.

This knowledge graph describes films and their metadata; each movie entity is characterized by attributes such as title, director, release year, a unique movie identifier, production budget (in millions), and worldwide gross revenue.

A knowledge graph of book club records and selections, describing books discussed or tracked by a book club. Main entities are book-club entries/books with attributes such as book title, author or editor, book club identifier, category/genre, publisher, publication year, and result (e.g., outcome or review).

A knowledge graph of people (individuals) describing personal and civic attributes. Key entities are persons and key attributes include name, age, party affiliation, electoral district, and a unique person identifier, which are commonly selected or filtered in queries.

Knowledge graph about people involved in debate events, describing participants and their roles within specific debates. Key entities are debate participants and debate events, with attributes for participant side (affirmative or negative), debate identifier, outcome indicator (whether the affirmative side won), and reference links tying participants to affirmative/negative roles.
This knowledge graph describes debate events as its primary entities. Each debate is characterized by attributes such as its date, debate identifier, venue, audience size, and class/type information.

This knowledge graph describes rounds (e.g., event or competition rounds) and the participants involved. Key entities are rounds and member/participant records, with important attributes including round identifiers, member identifiers and referenced member identifiers, each participant’s rank within the round, and a decoration/theme attribute.

This knowledge graph describes higher-education colleges and their basic metadata. Each college entity is represented with attributes such as a unique college identifier, official name, geographic location, leader name (e.g., president/principal), and institutional type/classification.

This KG describes members of an organization, representing each member as an entity. Key attributes include member name, member identifier, country, college affiliation identifier, and a referenced college identifier.

This knowledge graph contains records about head entities (individual persons). Each head is described by attributes such as name, age, place or state of birth, a unique identifier, and class/type information.

This knowledge graph describes organizational departments and their characteristics. Each department entity includes attributes such as name and identifier, creation date, number of employees, budget (in billions), and ranking.

This knowledge graph models organizational management information, recording departments and their leadership assignments. Main entities are management records, departments, and heads (people), with key attributes including department ID, head ID, reference IDs for department and head, and a temporary/acting status indicator.

This knowledge graph contains address records describing locations and contact addresses. Each address entity includes a unique address identifier, descriptive address details (e.g., street, city, etc.), and a type/classification that queries would commonly select or filter by.

A knowledge graph of product-supplier relationships and purchase records, describing which suppliers provide which products. Each supply record links a product and a supplier and includes identifiers, supply start and end dates, total amount purchased, and total purchase value.

This knowledge graph represents staff-to-department assignment records within an organization. Each assignment links a staff member to a department and includes attributes such as staff identifier, department identifier, job title code, assignment start and end dates, and references to related staff and department entities.

This knowledge graph describes customer orders in a commerce domain, representing order records and their links to customers. Key attributes include customer ID and reference customer ID, order ID, order date, and order status code, which support identification, association, and status-based filtering.

This knowledge graph describes department stores and their parent store chains. It contains individual store and chain entities with key attributes including store and chain identifiers, references linking stores to chains, store name, postal address, phone number, and email.

A knowledge graph of customer-address records linking customers to physical addresses; each record includes an address identifier, a customer identifier, optional reference identifiers, and a validity period (start and end dates). It is intended for queries that filter or select records by customer or address IDs, reference IDs, and date ranges.

This knowledge graph describes suppliers and vendor records within a supply-domain dataset. Each supplier entity includes key attributes used for lookup and filtering: a supplier identifier, supplier name, supplier phone number, and categorical/type classifications.
A knowledge graph of business customers, representing individual customer records; key attributes include customer ID, customer code, customer name, address, email, phone and payment method code.

This knowledge graph represents products in a retail/catalog domain. Each product entity is described by key attributes such as a unique product identifier, product name, product price, and a product type or category code, along with class/type annotations.

This knowledge graph describes order items in an e-commerce/order-management domain, where each entity represents a line item linking an order and a product. Key attributes include the order item ID, order ID, product ID, and references to the associated order and product.

A knowledge graph describing staff of an organization, where the primary entities are individual staff members; each staff entity is characterized by attributes such as staff ID, name, gender, and categorical type information.

This knowledge graph describes supplier address records that link suppliers to specific address entries. Each record includes identifiers for the address and supplier, optional reference IDs, and validity dates (start and end) that can be used to filter or select addresses by supplier, address identifier, and time period.

This knowledge graph covers department store chains in the retail domain, representing individual chains as the primary entities. For each chain it records key attributes including a unique chain identifier, the chain’s name, and type/classification metadata suitable for filtering or selection by ID or name.

This knowledge graph describes departments in organizations or retail stores. Each department entity includes attributes such as a department identifier, department name, associated store identifier, a reference store identifier, and a type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes retail shops/stores and their basic metadata. Each shop entity is characterized by attributes such as shop name and identifier, location, and opening information (opening date and opening year).

This knowledge graph describes inventory (stock) of devices across retail locations, with each stock record linking a device to a shop. Key entities are stock entries (records), devices, and shops, and important attributes include device identifiers, shop identifiers, quantities on hand, and reference identifiers that link stock records to the corresponding device and shop.

This knowledge graph describes devices and their software/network characteristics. Key entities are individual devices, each annotated with attributes such as installed applications, carrier/operator, device model, device identifier, software platform, and package/version information.

Knowledge graph of document sections and their parent documents, representing each section as an entity tied to a document. Key attributes include document code and reference document code, section code and section id, section sequence (ordering), and section title.

This knowledge graph describes document structure types used to organize documents; each entity represents a document structure or document type. Key attributes include a unique structure code, a human-readable description, a parent structure code indicating hierarchical relationships, and the entity's type/class.

This knowledge graph describes user accounts in an application domain, capturing individual users and their role associations. Key attributes for each user include user ID, login name, display name, password, role code, and references to role records.

This knowledge graph describes metadata for documents in a document management context, where each entity represents a document. Key attributes available for filtering or selection include document name, document code, document type and structure codes (and referenced structure codes), and access count (usage/popularity).

A knowledge graph of image metadata for a multimedia repository, describing individual image records and their classifications. Each image entity includes key attributes such as a unique identifier, name, URL, alternative (alt) text, and type/classification.

This knowledge graph models relationships between documents and organizational or functional areas, representing documents, functional areas, and the associations between them. Key attributes include document codes, functional-area codes, reference document and reference functional-area codes, and type/classification information.

This knowledge graph models associations between document sections and their images within a document corpus. It represents entities for sections and images and records key attributes and cross‑references such as image identifiers, section identifiers, and reference links between images and sections.

This knowledge graph models organizational functional areas, where each functional-area entity is described by a unique functional area code, a textual description, an optional parent functional area code indicating hierarchical relationships, and a type classification.

A knowledge graph of roles and role-related metadata, representing individual role entities (organizational or functional roles). Each role record includes key attributes such as a role code identifier, a textual role description, and a role type/classification that queries commonly select or filter on.

A knowledge graph of veterinary dog treatments, with primary entities for treatment events, dogs, and veterinary professionals. Each treatment record includes attributes such as treatment ID, date of treatment, cost, treatment type code, and references linking the treatment to the specific dog and professional.

This knowledge graph describes size records and standardized size categories for items, where each entity represents a size entry. Key attributes include a size code, a human-readable size description, and classification by type.

This knowledge graph describes charge records (individual charges) and their associated metadata. Key entities are charge items, with important attributes including a unique charge identifier, a charge amount, and a charge type/classification.

A knowledge graph of professionals and their contact and role information. Each professional entity includes identifiers and personal attributes (first name, last name, professional ID, role code), contact details (email address, cell number, home phone) and address fields (street, city, state, zip code).

A knowledge graph of owner records describing individual persons (owners), with key attributes including owner ID, first and last name, email address, cell and home phone numbers, and full mailing address information (street, city, state, ZIP code).

Knowledge graph of dogs in an adoption/shelter registry, describing individual animals and their lifecycle events. Each dog entity includes identifiers and attributes such as name and dog ID, breed and breed code, age and date of birth, gender, weight and size (and size code), arrival/adoption/departure dates, abandoned status, and owner/owner-reference information.
A knowledge graph about animal breeds: entities represent individual breeds and include key attributes such as breed code and breed name, along with type/classification information.

A knowledge graph of treatment types (categories of medical or clinical interventions) whose primary entities are individual treatment-type records; each record is described by a standardized code and a human-readable description and is associated with broader classification/type information.

This knowledge graph represents university/college students as the primary entities, capturing individual student records. Key attributes include student ID, first and last name, age, sex, major, advisor, and city code, which are commonly selected or used for filtering.

This knowledge graph describes relationships between dormitories and their amenities, with entities representing dorms, amenity items, and association records linking a dorm to an amenity. Key attributes include amenity identifiers, dormitory identifiers, cross-reference IDs for the amenity and dorm, and a classification/type for each association.

This KG describes student housing assignments, capturing which students live in which dorms and specific rooms. Key entities are residence records linking students and dorms, with important attributes including student identifier, dorm identifier, room number, and reference links to the student and dorm records.

This knowledge graph describes dormitory amenities, listing individual amenity items associated with student housing. Each amenity entity includes attributes such as a unique identifier, a human-readable name, and its category/type.

This knowledge graph describes university dormitories and student housing. Each dormitory is represented as an entity with key attributes including dorm name, a unique dorm identifier, gender designation (e.g., male/female/coed), and student capacity, along with class/type membership information.

This knowledge graph describes an organization's staff and personnel, with each entity representing an individual staff member. Key attributes include staff identifiers and address references, personal names (first, middle, last, nickname), date of birth, and employment dates (date joined and date left).

Knowledge graph of customer/CRM data describing individual customers and their records. Key entities are customers, with attributes such as customer ID, first and last name, contact details (phone, mobile, email), address identifiers, date of birth, date became customer, customer status code, and amount outstanding.

This knowledge graph describes customer payment transactions, representing individual payment records and their associated customers. Each payment record includes attributes such as payment amount, customer identifier (and reference customer identifier), payment method code, and payment timestamp.

Knowledge graph of postal address records describing physical locations. Each address entity includes a unique address identifier and common address attributes such as street/line 1 (number/building), city, state/province/county, ZIP/postcode, and country.

A knowledge graph of scheduled lessons and their associated participants and resources, including customers, staff/instructors, and vehicles. Each lesson record links these entities and exposes attributes such as lesson ID, customer/staff/vehicle identifiers, lesson date and time, lesson status code, and price.

A knowledge graph about vehicles, whose primary entities are individual vehicle records and their type/classification. Key attributes include unique vehicle identifiers, descriptive vehicle details (e.g., make, model, specifications), and type classification.

This knowledge graph describes student course enrolment records, representing individual enrollments that link students to courses. Each enrolment record includes attributes such as student identifier, course identifier, registration identifier, date of enrolment, date of completion, and references to the related student and course entities.

The knowledge graph represents student records in an educational environment, modeling individual students as the primary entities. Each student entity includes identifiers and account attributes (student ID, login name, password), personal name fields (given/ middle/ family name), and timestamps such as date of registration and date of latest logon.

This knowledge graph describes people who serve as course authors and tutors in an educational context. It represents individual authors/tutors and their key attributes, including unique author identifiers, personal/given/middle/family names, login credentials (login name and password), gender, postal address, and role/affiliation attributes relating to their author/tutor status.

This knowledge graph represents an educational course catalog, describing individual course entities. Key attributes include course identifiers, course name, course description, author identifiers (and author references) and subject identifiers (and subject references), which are commonly used to filter or retrieve course records.

This knowledge graph describes records of students' test-taking events, representing individual student test attempts. Each record captures attributes such as the date the test was taken, registration identifiers (primary and reference), the test result, and the record/type classification.

A knowledge graph of subjects (e.g., academic courses or topical categories), where the primary entities are individual subjects and their classifications. Key attributes include a subject identifier, the subject name, and the subject’s type or category.

This knowledge graph describes elections and elected officials, including candidates, delegates, committees, and the offices or districts they represent. Key attributes include committee membership, counties represented, delegate status, electoral district, party affiliation, election identifier, and first-elected date.

Knowledge graph about political parties and their candidates/officeholders over time; each party record includes the party name and identifier, the election year, and the party’s candidates or officeholders for positions such as governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, comptroller, and U.S. Senate.

This knowledge graph contains data about counties (administrative geographic divisions) as the primary entities. For each county it records identifiers, the county name, population counts, associated ZIP/postal codes, and type/classification information.

This knowledge graph contains data about political representatives (individual elected officials). Each representative entity is described by key attributes such as name, party affiliation, state, lifespan (dates/years), and a unique representative identifier.

This knowledge graph describes elections and election results, modeling individual election events and linked representatives/candidates. Key attributes include election identifiers, date, place, seats contested, vote counts and percentages, and representative identifiers (including reference IDs).

A knowledge graph describing retail shops, where each shop entity is characterized by attributes such as shop identifier, name, physical location and district, manager name, and number of products available. These attributes support queries filtering or selecting shops by location, district, manager, or inventory size.

This knowledge graph describes employee evaluation and award records within an organizational HR context. Each evaluation record represents an assessed employee and includes attributes such as bonus amount, employee identifier (and referenced employee identifier), the year awarded, and the record’s classification/type.

This knowledge graph models employees (personnel) and their records; the primary entities are employee instances. Key attributes available for filtering or selection include name, age, city (location), and employee identifier, along with classification/type information for each employee.

This knowledge graph describes hiring and employment relationships linking employees and shops. Main entities are employment records (relationships), employees, and shops, with key attributes including employee and shop identifiers, reference IDs to external employee/shop records, employment start dates, and full-time status.

This knowledge graph describes nominations of artworks at film/festival events, representing nomination records that link artworks to festivals. Each nomination includes key attributes such as artwork and festival identifiers (and their reference IDs) and the nomination result (e.g., winner, nominee), which are the primary queryable fields.
This knowledge graph describes artworks and their metadata. Each artwork entity is represented with key attributes such as a unique identifier, its name or title, and its type or classification.

This dataset describes festivals and their associated detail records, with individual festival events and organizational roles as the primary entities. Key attributes include festival name and identifier, location, year, chairperson name, and number of audience members, which are commonly used to filter or select records.

This knowledge graph describes entrepreneurship and startup funding, modeling entrepreneurs, their associated companies, and investors. Key attributes include company affiliation, investor relationships, amounts of money requested, and entrepreneur/people identifiers used to link records.

A knowledge graph about people that represents individual persons and their biographical and physical attributes. Key properties include name, date of birth, a unique person identifier, height, and weight.

Knowledge graph of user accounts and account records. It represents individual users/accounts as the main entities and provides attributes commonly queried such as account name, unique user identifier, and account type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes items (individual resources) in an inventory or catalog-like domain. Each item entity is represented with key attributes such as a unique identifier, a human-readable title, and a classification/type.

This knowledge graph represents trust relationships between users, modeling directed trust assertions from a source user to a target user. Each trust record includes key attributes such as source and target user identifiers, optional reference source/target identifiers, and a trust value (e.g., numeric or categorical) describing the strength or nature of the trust.

This knowledge graph describes consumer reviews of items, with review records that connect users and items. Each review record includes attributes such as numeric rating and rank, unique identifiers, the associated item and user IDs, and optional references to other item or user IDs.

This knowledge graph contains competition records documenting farms' participation and outcomes in competitions. Each record links a farm to a competition and includes key attributes such as competition identifier, farm identifier, the participant's rank, and reference links to the competition and farm entities.

Knowledge graph of cities/municipalities, describing individual city entities and their key attributes—official name, unique city identifier, population, area (km²), census ranking, and administrative status—suitable for selecting or filtering cities by these properties.

This knowledge graph describes agricultural farms with a focus on livestock inventories.
