Each farm entity includes attributes such as a farm identifier and year, individual animal counts (bulls, cows, oxen, pigs, sheep and goats) and aggregate measures like total cattle, total horses, and working horses.

This knowledge graph describes agricultural/farm competitions, representing individual competition events and their associated host cities and organizers. Each competition entity is characterized by identifiers, host city identifiers (and references), hosts, thematic topic, and year.

This knowledge graph contains records of film market estimations, representing estimation entries that link films and markets. Each estimation entry includes attributes such as an estimation identifier, film identifier, market identifier (and reference IDs), low and high estimates, year, and type.

This knowledge graph describes market entities, each representing a market in a value network; key attributes include the market's country, a unique market identifier, the number of cities it covers, and its type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes films (movies) as the primary entities, with key attributes including title, director, producing studio, a unique film identifier, and gross box-office revenue in US dollars.

Aviation-focused knowledge graph describing commercial flights and related entities. It represents flights, airlines, and airports with key attributes such as airline, flight number, source airport, destination airport, and links/references that associate flights with airline and airport records.

A knowledge graph of airports where the primary entities are individual airport records. Each airport is described by key attributes such as airport code, airport name, city, country, and country abbreviation, which are commonly used for filtering or selection.

This knowledge graph describes airline organizations and related airline entities. Each airline entity is characterized by properties such as official name, abbreviation/code, country of registration, a unique identifier, and a classification/type.

This knowledge graph describes airlines and airline companies as the primary entities, representing individual carriers and their metadata. For each airline it records attributes such as operational/active status, an internal identifier, callsign, country, IATA and ICAO codes, and the airline name.

This knowledge graph describes commercial flight routes, linking airlines to origin and destination airports. The primary entities are route records that record an airline (and airline ID), source and destination airports (and their IDs), a route identifier, codeshare status, and related reference identifiers.

This knowledge graph describes airports as the primary domain, representing individual airport entities and their locations. Key attributes include identifiers, airport name, city and country, IATA and ICAO codes, elevation, and geographic coordinates.

A knowledge graph of flight operations and records covering flights, airports, airlines (companies), pilots, and flight vehicles. Key attributes include flight identifiers and vehicle flight numbers, dates/timestamps, airport and company references, pilot information, and operational measurements such as altitude and velocity.

This knowledge graph describes airports and their related metadata. Each airport entity is characterized by attributes such as name, city, country, an internal identifier, and standard codes used for identification (IATA and ICAO).

Knowledge graph about operating companies and corporate entities, capturing company identities and corporate characteristics. Key entities are operating companies with attributes such as company identifier, name, legal type, jurisdiction or country of incorporation, principal business activities, and group equity shareholding (ownership stakes).

This knowledge graph describes motor-racing event results, representing individual race result records for drivers and constructors across races. Key entities include results, drivers, constructors and races, with attributes such as finishing position and position order/text, grid position, laps completed, points scored, race time and milliseconds, fastest lap (time and speed), rank/status, and identifiers linking results to specific drivers, constructors and races.

This KG describes racing events (motorsport races) and their associated circuits. Key entities are race events and circuits, with attributes such as race name, date and year, round number, race and circuit identifiers (including reference circuit IDs), race time, and event URL.

This KG contains data about motorsport constructors (racing teams), with entities representing individual constructor teams and key attributes including a unique identifier, a reference code, the team name, nationality, and a website URL. It is suitable for queries that filter or select constructors by name, nationality, id, or reference.

This knowledge graph describes motorsport circuits (race tracks) worldwide, representing individual circuit entities. Key attributes for each circuit include identifiers and reference codes, official name and URL, country and location, and geographic coordinates (latitude, longitude) plus altitude.

This knowledge graph models seasons as its primary entities (seasonal periods or editions), with key attributes including the year, an associated URL reference, and a type/classification. Typical use involves identifying or filtering season entities by year, inspecting their URL links, or checking their classification.

This knowledge graph describes motorsport constructor standings, recording results for racing teams (constructors) tied to specific races. The main entities are constructor-standings records that link constructors and races and provide attributes such as constructor and race identifiers, a standings identifier, points scored, numeric and textual finishing positions, and wins.

This knowledge graph describes drivers (individual people, typically motorsport drivers). Key entities are driver records with attributes such as forename and surname, date of birth, nationality, racing number, unique identifiers (driver ID, code, reference), and related URL metadata.

Knowledge graph describing motorsport team (constructor) race results, with records linking constructors (teams) to specific races. Each result record includes attributes such as constructor identifier, race identifier, points scored, result status, and unique result identifiers and references to the constructor and race.

This knowledge graph contains records describing statuses of items or processes. Each status entity includes attributes such as a status value (e.g., label or code), a status identifier, and a type/classification.

This knowledge graph models motorsport driver standings, capturing standings entries for drivers in races or seasons. Key entities are driver standings entries, drivers, and races, with attributes such as driver and standings identifiers, race identifiers, points, numeric position and position text, number of wins, and references linking to driver and race records.

This knowledge graph contains motorsport qualifying session results, describing each qualifying entry for a race with associated driver and constructor information. Key entities are qualifying entries, drivers, constructors, and races, with attributes such as car number, qualifying position, Q1/Q2/Q3 lap times, and identifiers linking entries to driver, constructor, and race records.

This knowledge graph describes student sports participation, modeling individual student-athlete records and their involvement in athletic programs. Key attributes include sport name, number of games played, hours per week spent in the sport, scholarship status, and student identifiers or references.

This knowledge graph contains academic student records and demographic information, representing individual students as the primary entities. Key attributes include advisor, age, city code, first name, last name, major, sex, and student ID.

A knowledge graph of student gameplay records linking students to the games they play. Each play record (entity) includes key attributes such as student identifier, game identifier (and reference links to those entities) and hours played.

Knowledge graph about video games, representing individual game entities. Each game is described by key attributes such as a unique game identifier, the game name, its type/genre, and classification, enabling retrieval or filtering of games by id, name, or type.

This knowledge graph models injury and accident records related to players in sporting events, capturing incidents that occur during games. Key entities are incident records, players, and games, with important attributes including record identifiers, game identifiers (and reference game IDs), injury details, number of matches affected, and source provenance.

This knowledge graph describes sports games/matches and related entities. Each game record includes key attributes such as a unique identifier, home and away teams, competition, date, season, stadium (and stadium ID), and the match score.

This knowledge graph describes sports stadiums/venues as the primary entities, with each stadium represented by identifiers and names. Key attributes include attendance metrics (average attendance and total attendance), capacity utilization (capacity percentage), and the number of home games.

A knowledge graph of companies and their corporate metadata and financials. It represents company entities with attributes such as company name and identifier, headquarters location, main industry, rank, market value, and financial metrics including assets, sales, and profits (reported in billions).

A knowledge graph of gas stations where the primary entities are individual stations described by key attributes such as station identifier, location, opening year, manager name, vice manager name, and representative name. It supports filtering and retrieval of stations based on location, operational year, staff roles, and station ID.

This knowledge graph describes associations between stations and companies, representing records that link station entities with company entities. Each record includes attributes such as company identifier, station identifier, reference identifiers for the company and station, and a yearly rank value indicating the company's rank for that year.

This knowledge graph describes gymnasts and their competition results; each gymnast entity includes identifiers and reference IDs plus numeric scores for individual apparatus (floor exercise, pommel horse, rings, vault, parallel bars, horizontal bar) and an aggregated total points value.
A knowledge graph about people (individuals) and their personal information. Each person entity is characterized by attributes such as name, age, height, hometown, and an identifier (people_id).

This knowledge graph describes healthcare appointment records, capturing scheduled visits and their associated participants. Each appointment entity includes key attributes such as an appointment identifier, start and end times, links to the patient, physician and prep nurse involved, and the examination room.

A knowledge graph of professional affiliations in the healthcare domain, describing records that link physicians to organizational units and indicate their primary affiliations. Key entities are affiliation records, physicians, and departments, with important attributes including department membership, physician identity, primary-affiliation status, and references to associated physicians or departments.

This knowledge graph describes medical procedure events that patients undergo during hospital stays, linking each event to the patient, attending physician, assisting nurse, and the procedures performed. Key attributes available for filtering or selection include patient identity, physician, assisting nurse, procedure details, associated hospital stay, and date of the procedure.

This knowledge graph represents healthcare patient records, with individual patients as the primary entities. Key attributes include personal identifiers and contact details (name, address, phone, SSN), insurance identifiers, and primary care provider information (including references to provider records).

This knowledge graph describes training and certification records in a clinical/medical context, centering on physicians, their training events, and the treatments associated with that training. Key attributes include certification date and expiration, the physician involved, and links/references to specific physician and treatment entities.

This knowledge graph describes rooms in a building or campus, representing individual room entities and their location and characteristics. Key attributes include block code, floor (and combined block-floor reference), room number, room type, and availability/unavailability status.

This knowledge graph describes medications and drug products: the primary entities are medication records, each annotated with attributes such as name, brand, code (identifier), descriptive text, and type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes physicians as the primary entities (individual medical staff). Each physician record includes identifying and employment attributes such as employee ID, full name, job position, social security number, and classification/category.

A knowledge graph of hospital nursing on-call assignments, modeling on-call shifts for nursing staff and their association with hospital blocks and floors. Each on-call assignment records the assigned nurse, on-call start and end times, block code and block floor, and links to the corresponding nurse and block entities.

This knowledge graph covers healthcare stay records (patient admissions) and related entities, primarily stays, patients, and rooms. Each stay links to a patient and a room and carries key attributes such as a stay identifier, start and end timestamps, and references to patient and room records.

This knowledge graph describes procedures (e.g., medical or service procedures) as the primary entities, recording for each procedure an identification code, a human-readable name, a monetary cost, and a classification/type. It supports finding and comparing procedures by code, name, cost, or type.

A knowledge graph of medical prescriptions and related clinical orders, capturing prescriptions issued by physicians to patients and their associated appointments. Key entities are prescriptions, patients, physicians, medications, and appointments, with important attributes including medication, dose, prescription date, and references/identifiers linking to patient, physician, medication, and appointment records.

This knowledge graph describes organizational departments as the primary entities. For each department it records key attributes such as a department identifier, the department name, the department head (person) and a reference linking to that head, as well as the department's classification/type.

Knowledge graph about nursing staff in healthcare settings, representing individual nurses as the primary entities with key attributes such as employee identifier, full name, job position, professional registration status, and social security number.

This knowledge graph contains data about building or structural blocks, where the primary entities are individual block instances. Each block is described by attributes such as a block code identifier, the block's floor or level, and its type/classification, which are commonly used for filtering or selecting blocks.

This knowledge graph represents an employee directory and HR roster containing individual employee records. Each employee entity includes attributes such as employee ID, first and last name, email, phone number, hire date, job and department identifiers (with links to job/department records), manager ID, salary, and commission percentage.

This knowledge graph describes geographic location and address records. Its primary entities are locations, each annotated with attributes such as a location identifier, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country identifier, and referenced country identifier.
This KG describes countries: each country entity includes attributes such as a country identifier, the country name, and references to a region (region ID/reference), along with type/class metadata.

A knowledge graph of organizational departments within an enterprise, where the primary entities are department records. Each department is described by key attributes such as department identifier, department name, location identifier, manager identifier, and its type/classification.

This knowledge graph represents job postings: each job entity includes a unique identifier, a job title, minimum and maximum salary values, and type/class metadata, enabling queries that select or filter by job id, job title, min_salary, and max_salary.

This knowledge graph describes geographical regions; the primary entities are individual regions, characterized by attributes such as a region identifier, a region name, and their class/type membership.

This knowledge graph describes authors (individual persons) as the primary domain entities. Each author is represented with attributes such as an author identifier, first/given name, last/family name, and a classification/type label.

A knowledge graph of scholarly authorship that represents authors, academic papers, and affiliated institutions. Each authorship record links an author and their institution to a paper and records attributes such as author identifier, author order, institution identifier, paper identifier, and references to related author/institution/paper identifiers.

This knowledge graph describes institutions and organizations, capturing individual institutional entities. Each institution is described by attributes such as its name, a unique identifier, country (location), and its classification or type.

This knowledge graph represents academic research papers as entities and their associated metadata. Key attributes available for filtering or selection include each paper's identifier, title, and assigned type or category.

Knowledge graph of lodging reservations, describing individual booking records. Each reservation includes guest details (first and last name), stay dates (check-in and check-out), occupancy (adults and kids), assigned room or room reference, booking code, and rate.

Knowledge graph about hotel or accommodation rooms, where each room is represented as an entity. Key attributes include base price, number of beds, bed type, decor, maximum occupancy, room identifier, and room name.

This knowledge graph describes insurance policy records and their relationships to customers. Each policy entity includes attributes such as policy identifier, customer identifier (and referenced customer id), policy type code, and start and end dates.

This KG contains insurance claim header records and their associated policies, representing individual claims and basic policy links. Each claim record includes identifiers and attributes such as claimed amount, paid amount, claim header ID, claim status and type codes, date of claim, date of settlement, and policy identifiers (including referenced policy IDs).

This knowledge graph models claims processing in the insurance/claims-management domain, representing claim-processing records, individual claims, and associated staff. Key attributes include claim identifiers, processing and stage identifiers, outcome codes, and references linking records to related claims and staff members.

This knowledge graph describes claim-related documents in a claims/insurance processing domain, representing individual document records associated with claims. Key attributes for each document include the claim identifier, the staff member who created it (creator staff ID), the creation date, the document type code, and references to related claim IDs and their creating staff.

This knowledge graph describes customer records, representing individual customers as the primary entities. Each customer entity includes key attributes such as a customer identifier (ID), detailed customer information, and type/class annotations.

This knowledge graph models claim processing stages within claim lifecycle management, representing individual stage entities and their progression. Each stage entity includes attributes such as a stage identifier, status name and description, a reference to the next stage, and type classification.

This knowledge graph describes staff members in an organization, representing individual employee entities. Key attributes include staff identifiers, descriptive staff details (e.g., personal or role-related information), and class/type information about each staff entity.

Knowledge graph about first notifications of loss in the insurance domain, representing FNOL (claim) records and associated services. Each record includes key identifiers and attributes such as FNOL ID, customer ID, policy ID, service ID, and reference links between customers, policies, and services.

This knowledge graph models relationships between customers and their policies, representing records that link customer entities to policy entities. Key attributes include customer identifiers, policy identifiers, reference IDs for customers and policies, and policy lifecycle dates such as date opened and date closed.

This knowledge graph describes available insurance policies and related policy records. Each policy entity includes key attributes such as policy identifier, policy type code, customer phone number, and classification/type information for filtering or identification.

This knowledge graph describes customers for an organization, representing individual customer entities. Each customer record includes key attributes such as a customer identifier, customer name, and categorical type/class membership.

This knowledge graph represents financial and legal settlement records and their associated claims. Its primary entities are settlement and claim records, with key attributes including claim identifiers (and reference claim identifiers), settlement identifiers, settlement amounts, and effective dates.

A knowledge graph of insurance claims where the primary entities are individual claim records; each claim is described by identifiers (claim ID, FNOL ID, reference FNOL ID), an effective date, and classification/type metadata. The data supports tracking, linking, and filtering claims and their associated first-notice-of-loss events.

This knowledge graph describes service offerings; its primary entities are individual services. Each service is characterized by an identifier, a human‑readable name, and a classification/type that can be used to filter, group, or select services.

This knowledge graph contains records of customer policies, representing individual policy instances associated with customers. Each policy record includes attributes such as customer identifiers (and referenced customer IDs), policy identifiers, policy type codes, and start and end dates.

This knowledge graph contains insurance claim records as its primary entities, each representing an individual claim. For each claim it captures identifiers and policy associations (claim ID, policy ID, reference policy ID) along with key attributes such as amount claimed, amount settled, date the claim was made, and date the claim was settled.

This knowledge graph describes payment transactions and settlement records in the payments/financial domain. Key entities are individual payment records and their associated settlements, with important attributes including payment amount, date payment was made, unique payment identifier, payment method code, and settlement (or settlement reference) identifiers.

This knowledge graph describes insurance claim settlements, representing settlement records, claims, and associated customer policies. Each record includes identifiers (claim ID, settlement ID, reference claim ID, customer policy ID), monetary amounts claimed and settled, and dates for when the claim was made and when it was settled.

This knowledge graph describes customers in a business context, with each entity representing an individual customer record. Key attributes available for queries include customer identifiers, detailed customer information (e.g., profile or account details), and entity type/classification metadata.

This knowledge graph contains data about editors (editor profiles) and the individuals who serve in editorial roles. Key attributes for these editor entities include name, age, a unique editor identifier, and classification/type information.

This knowledge graph describes journal editorial committees, modeling membership records that link editors to academic journals. Each record captures key attributes such as editor identifiers, journal identifiers, referenced editor and journal identifiers, and a work_type indicating the editor's role or type of contribution.

A knowledge graph describing journals/publications, where the primary entities are individual journal records. Each record includes key attributes such as publication date, a journal identifier, sales figures, thematic category, and its resource/class type.

A knowledge graph about banking that represents bank branches (or banks) as the primary entities. Each branch is described by key attributes such as branch name, branch identifier, city and state location, and number of customers.

This knowledge graph describes banking customers and their account relationships. Main entities are individual customers (identified by customer ID and name) with key attributes such as account balance, account type, branch ID (and reference branch ID), credit score, number of loans, and state.

This knowledge graph models banking loan records, with individual loans as the primary entities. Key attributes include loan identifier, loan amount, loan type, associated customer identifier, issuing branch identifier, and reference links to the related customer and branch records.

This knowledge graph describes records of services associated with residents, linking residents, services, and properties. Each record captures key attributes such as resident and service identifiers, property identifier, dates (moved-in, service requested, service provided) and other descriptive details.

A knowledge graph of organizations and their hierarchical relationships, representing organization records and how they are grouped or report to one another. Each organization entity includes an identifier, a parent-organization identifier (for hierarchy), descriptive details, and classification/type information.

The knowledge graph represents time-stamped location records for tracked physical things (e.g., devices or assets). Each record links a thing identifier (and optional referenced thing identifier) to a date/time, a location code, and a classification/type attribute.

This knowledge graph contains records of customer event notes linking residents to property-related events and service interactions. Key entities are customer events/notes, residents, and properties, with important attributes including customer event ID, customer event note ID, resident ID, property ID, move-in date, references to related events, and service type code.

This knowledge graph describes services offered or managed by organizations, with primary entities for service records and the organizations that provide or reference them. Key attributes include organization identifiers and referenced organization identifiers, service identifiers, service type codes, and descriptive service details.

A knowledge graph of items and service records associated with organizations, describing which organizations are linked to particular things and the services related to them. Key entities are things/service records and organizations, with primary attributes including thing identifiers, organization and reference-organization identifiers, service details, service-type codes, and type-of-thing codes.

This KG describes time-stamped status records for items ("things"), tracking the status of physical or logical objects over time. Key entities are individual things and their status records, with important attributes including thing_id, ref-thing_id, status_of_thing_code, date_and_date, and the record/type classification.

This KG describes customer event records for housing/property move-ins, linking events to customers, residents, properties and related items. Key attributes include event identifiers, customer and resident IDs, property IDs, date_moved_in, thing IDs, and various reference IDs used for filtering and selection.

This knowledge graph describes real estate properties, with entities representing individual property records. Key attributes include property identifier, property address, property type code (classification), and other descriptive details that users would filter or select.

This knowledge graph describes customers and their records; the primary entities are individual customer instances. Key attributes available for queries include customer identifiers, customer details (e.g., profile or contact information), and type/class annotations for each customer.

This knowledge graph describes property residency and occupancy records, linking residents to the properties they occupy. Key entities are resident/occupancy records and properties, with important attributes including resident IDs, property IDs (and reference property IDs), move-in and move-out dates, and other residency details.

This knowledge graph models participation relationships between events and participants, i.e., records linking individual participants to specific events. Each record contains key attributes such as event identifier, participant identifier, optional reference event/participant identifiers, and type/classification metadata that are typically used for filtering or selection.

This knowledge graph describes events and their relationships to services, where each event entity has an identifier, descriptive details, a classification/type, and links to related service identifiers (including primary and referenced service IDs). Typical attributes for selection or filtering are event_id, event details, service_id, ref-service_id, and event type.

A knowledge graph of participants in a value network or registry, representing individual or organizational participants and their classifications. Key attributes include a participant identifier, a participant type code (role/category), and descriptive details about each participant.

This knowledge graph describes service records and their classifications within a service domain. Each service entity includes attributes such as a unique service identifier, a service type code, and type/class information used to categorize services.

This knowledge graph represents customer cross-reference information used to map master customer identities to external or referenced customer identifiers across source systems. Each cross-reference entity includes attributes such as a cross-reference ID, the master customer ID, the referenced (external) customer ID, the source system code, and a type/classification.

This knowledge graph contains records about business rates (local business tax/valuation) entries and their classifications. Key entities are business-rates records, with important attributes including a business-rates identifier, CMI cross-reference identifiers (and reference cross-reference fields), and type/classification labels for filtering and linking records.

This knowledge graph describes council tax records, with each entity representing a council tax account or entry. Key attributes include a council tax identifier, CMI cross-reference identifiers (and referenced CMI cross-ref ids) and type metadata for each record.

This KG models electoral register records (voter or registration entries) and their associated metadata. Key attributes are persistent identifiers and linking fields, such as an electoral register ID and cross-reference IDs (including CMI cross-reference and reference cross-reference), along with type annotations.

This knowledge graph contains records of benefit overpayment cases, representing individual overpayment incidents or claims. Key entities are overpayment records and their associated identifiers, with important attributes including cross‑reference IDs to case management systems, council tax identifiers, reference cross‑reference IDs, and type/class information.

This knowledge graph represents a customer master index for managing customer records and their classifications. Its primary entities are customer master records, with key attributes including the master customer identifier, detailed customer information (customer details), and type/classification metadata.

A knowledge graph of rent arrears cases, representing individual arrears records and their classifications. Key attributes include CMI cross-reference identifiers, reference CMI IDs, council tax identifiers, and type/class labels that are commonly used to filter or select records.

This knowledge graph contains records of parking fines and related enforcement entries, with the primary entities being individual parking-fine notices. Each record includes key identifiers and reference attributes—such as CMI cross-reference IDs, council tax IDs, and related reference IDs—along with type/classification metadata.

This KG describes repair assignment records that link machines, repair jobs, and technicians in a maintenance context. Each assignment entity records identifiers and reference links for the machine, the repair task, and the technician (e.g., machine_id, repair_id, technician_id and associated reference fields).

This knowledge graph describes machines and their characteristics. Each machine entity is described by attributes such as class/type, a unique machine identifier, series, manufacturing year, quality rank, associated team, and value points, which can be used for filtering and selection.

This knowledge graph describes technicians (personnel) as the primary domain entities, with key attributes including name, age, starting year (employment start), team affiliation, and a unique technician identifier. It is suitable for retrieving or filtering technicians by their personal details, employment start date, team membership, and ID.

This knowledge graph describes repair and maintenance records for assets and repair events. Each repair entity is characterized by attributes such as a unique repair identifier, a name, a launch/start date, free-text notes, and a classification/type.

A knowledge graph of product catalog data for retail or inventory contexts. It represents individual products and their attributes, notably product code, name, manufacturer (and references to manufacturer records), and price.

This knowledge graph describes manufacturers (manufacturing companies) and related company-level entities. Key attributes include company code/identifier, name, founder, headquarters location, and revenue, enabling identification and comparison of manufacturers.

A knowledge graph about furniture, representing individual pieces of furniture as the primary entities and recording key attributes such as a furniture identifier, name, market rate (price), number of components, and their type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes furniture manufacturing data, representing furniture items, manufacturers, and the relationships between them. Each record includes attributes such as furniture identifiers, manufacturer identifiers, price in dollars, and reference IDs linking furniture to manufacturer entries.

This knowledge graph describes manufacturers (manufacturing companies) and their basic facts. For each manufacturer it records identifiers and name plus attributes such as number of factories, number of shops, and year opened.

A knowledge graph about countries and related geographic/political information. It contains country entities with key attributes such as country identifier, country name, capital city, official/native language, and entity classification/type.

A knowledge graph of athletes (players) that records individual players and their team affiliations, identifiers, and reference teams. It captures key attributes for each player such as years played and match performance statistics, including singles, doubles, and total win–loss records.

This knowledge graph describes sports match-season records, covering entities such as players, teams, seasons, countries and colleges. Key attributes include season and team affiliation, player position, college and country of origin, draft class and draft pick number, and links to referenced teams or countries.

This knowledge graph models teams within an organization as the primary entities, with each team described by attributes such as a human-readable name and a unique team identifier. Teams are also annotated with class/type information used to categorize or filter them.

A knowledge graph of medicines where entities represent individual pharmaceutical drugs; key attributes include unique identifiers, generic (official) names, trade/brand names, regulatory approval status (e.g., FDA-approved), and medicine type/classification. These attributes are the primary fields used to select or filter medicines in queries.

This knowledge graph covers pharmacological relationships between medicines and enzymes, modeling interaction records that connect specific medicine entities to enzyme entities. Each interaction includes key attributes such as medicine and enzyme identifiers, the type of interaction (e.g., inhibition, metabolism), and reference identifiers for the medicine and enzyme.

Biomedical knowledge graph about enzymes (genes/proteins) and their disease associations. It describes enzyme entities with attributes such as identifiers and names, chromosome and cellular locations, enzymatic products, OMIM disease links, and porphyria-related annotations.

A knowledge graph of mountains and related geographic features, where the primary entities are individual mountains. Each mountain is described by attributes such as name and identifier, physical measures (height and prominence), and geographic context (range and country).

Knowledge graph of photographs, focusing on photos related to mountains; main entities include photo records, mountains, and camera lenses. Each photo is described by attributes such as a unique identifier, name, color, and references/links to the associated mountain and camera lens.

This knowledge graph describes camera lenses as the primary entities, with each lens characterized by attributes such as brand, name, identifier (id), focal length in millimeters, and maximum aperture; queries typically filter or select lenses by these properties.

This knowledge graph describes museums as entities, providing key information about each museum; important attributes include a unique museum identifier, the museum's name, number of staff, year opened, and its classification/type.

This knowledge graph describes visitors (a directory of people interacting with a service), modeling each visitor as an entity with attributes such as a unique identifier, name, age, level of membership, and entity type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes museum visit records, linking visitors and museums as primary entities and representing each visit with attributes such as museum identifier, visitor identifier, number of tickets purchased, total amount spent, and links to the referenced museum and visitor. It supports filtering or aggregation of visits by museum, visitor, ticket count, or spending.

This knowledge graph describes songs and related musical recordings, with primary entities representing songs and their artists. Key attributes include song name, artist name, country, genre, language(s), release date, rating, unique identifiers and reference identifiers, and media resolution.

A knowledge graph of digital media files (primarily audio tracks), where the main entities are individual file/media items described by attributes such as artist name (and reference artist), duration, file identifier, file size, and available formats.

This knowledge graph describes musical artists; the primary entities are artists annotated with attributes such as artist name, country (of origin), gender, preferred musical genre, and a reference linking to that genre.

A knowledge graph of entertainment genres, treating individual genres as the primary entities. For each genre it records attributes such as the genre name, the region or place where it is most popular, a rating score, and classification labels (type).

This knowledge graph describes artists and their works, representing individual artists and providing attributes such as age, artist name, a unique artist identifier, and metadata about notable releases (famous title and famous release date).

This knowledge graph models music festivals, with main entities representing individual festival events. Each event is described by attributes such as festival name, category, date of ceremony, unique identifier, result or outcome, and linked volume/reference-volume metadata.

This knowledge graph models music chart volume entries and recordings, linking songs to their performing artists and chart volumes. Key attributes include artist identifiers (and referenced/featured artist IDs), song title, issue date and volume/issue identifiers, and metrics such as weeks on top.

A knowledge graph of high school students and their basic records. Main entities are individual highschoolers, with key attributes including name, identifier (ID), grade level, and their classification/type.

A knowledge graph of student friendship records: the main entities are friendship entries that link students and their friends. Key attributes include the friendship record identifier, the student identifier, the friend identifier, and reference fields that point to the related student or friend entities.

This knowledge graph models "likes" relationships in a social/preferences domain, recording which students express likes for particular items. Primary entities are like records that link student entities to liked items, with key attributes including student identifiers, liked-item identifiers, and reference identifiers that associate likes with students and items.

Knowledge graph of people and their social connections, modeling individuals and friendships. Each person entity includes attributes such as name, links to friend entities (and reference identifiers or reference names for those friends), and a year field associated with the person or the friendship.
A knowledge graph about people (individuals), representing each person as a primary entity. Key attributes include name, age, gender, city of residence, and job/occupation.

This knowledge graph describes journalists, representing individual journalist entities in the domain of journalism. Key attributes for each journalist include name, a unique journalist identifier, age, nationality, and years of working (professional experience).

This knowledge graph covers journalism and news reporting, representing news report records and their links to events and journalists. Each report entity includes attributes such as event identifiers, journalist identifiers, references to other events or journalists, and a work type that classifies the kind of report.
A knowledge graph about events and their metadata. It represents event entities with key attributes including date, attendance (or attendance count), unique event identifier, name, and venue.

This knowledge graph describes hosts (individual people who present or host programs or events), with host entities characterized by key attributes such as a unique identifier, name, age, nationality, and classification/type information.

This knowledge graph describes party events as entities, recording for each event its first and last year (temporal span), location, number of hosts, theme, and a unique identifier. These attributes are the primary fields used for selection and filtering.

This knowledge graph models event hosting relationships, describing parties (events) and the hosts assigned to them as primary entities. Each host-party assignment includes attributes such as host and party identifiers, a flag indicating whether the host is the main person in charge, and reference IDs linking to the host and party records.

This knowledge graph models events associated with parties or organizations, representing individual event records and their links to the organizing party and the responsible member. Key attributes for each event include an event identifier, event name, party identifier, member-in-charge identifier, and reference links to the corresponding party and member records.

This knowledge graph describes political parties and their associated officeholders, including ministers and regional affiliations. It records key attributes such as party identifiers and names, region references, ministerial appointments, and office tenure details (took office and left office).

This knowledge graph describes regions as the primary domain, representing individual region records and identifiers. Each region is characterized by attributes such as region identifier, region name and label, along with metadata fields like catalogue, date, and format that are commonly used for filtering or selection.

This knowledge graph describes individual political members or representatives of a legislative or governing body. Each member entity is characterized by attributes such as personal name and unique member ID, current in‑office status, and party affiliation identifiers (including referenced party IDs).

This knowledge graph describes attendance records of members at performances, capturing which members participated in which performances. Each attendance record includes member identifiers, performance identifiers, the number of pieces performed, and optional reference identifiers linking to the member and to the performance.

This knowledge graph describes performances (live events) and related event metadata. For each performance it records key attributes such as attendance figures, date, host, location, and a unique performance identifier.

This knowledge graph describes members of an organization or group, representing individual people or entities as the primary objects. Each member record includes attributes such as a member identifier, name, nationality, role within the organization, and an entity type/classification.

Knowledge graph about people, representing individual persons with identifiers and personal attributes. Key attributes include name and people ID, as well as physical characteristics (height, weight) and hometown information.

Knowledge graph of perpetrators involved in violent incidents or attacks, representing individual perpetrator records. Each perpetrator entity includes attributes such as country, location, incident date/year, numbers injured and killed, and identifier fields linking to people or perpetrator records (IDs and reference IDs).

This knowledge graph describes student profiles and related academic/personal information. Key entities are individual students, with attributes including advisor, age, city code (location), first name, last name, major, sex, and student identifier.

This knowledge graph models records of pets associated with students, representing ownership or association instances that link student and pet entities. Key attributes include pet identifiers, student identifiers, reference IDs that link to pets or students, and a type/classification for each record.
A knowledge graph about pets, representing individual pet records as entities. Each pet has attributes such as age, a unique identifier, type (species/breed), weight, and classification information.

This knowledge graph catalogs chip models, with entities representing individual semiconductor or embedded device models. Each model is described by key attributes such as model name, launch year, RAM (MiB), ROM (MiB), available slots, and connectivity features (Wi‑Fi and Bluetooth).

This knowledge graph describes mobile phones and related device models and manufacturers. It contains phone entities annotated with attributes such as company/manufacturer name, chip model and hardware model name, screen mode (and screen-mode references), accreditation type and level, and associated dates.

This knowledge graph describes screen/display modes for computer systems and devices. It represents individual screen mode records with attributes such as character cell dimensions, pixel resolution, graphics mode, hardware color capabilities, color/map information, memory used (KB), and mode type.

Knowledge graph about phone marketplace inventory and availability, representing records that link mobile phones to specific markets. Each record describes the phone and market identifiers, the number of units in stock, and reference IDs that connect to phone and market records.

This knowledge graph describes mobile phones as its primary entities and their associated device records. Key attributes include model/name, carrier, memory size (in GB), a unique phone identifier, and price, which are commonly used for filtering and selection.

This knowledge graph describes physical or commercial markets, representing individual market entities and their characteristics. Each market is described by attributes such as district (location), a market identifier, number of employees, number of shops, and an overall ranking.

This knowledge graph describes people (individuals) and information about them. Key attributes include name, birth date, height, nationality, and a unique person identifier, which are commonly selected or used to filter query results.

This knowledge graph describes poker players and their tournament-related records. Key entities are individual poker players, with attributes and identifiers such as total earnings, best finish, number of final tables made, money rank, and linked person/poker-player IDs.

This knowledge graph models a product catalog, describing catalog entries and inventory items. Each entry includes identifiers and names, hierarchical relations and catalog-level numbers (parent/previous/next), stock numbers, physical attributes (height, width, length, capacity), and prices quoted in dollars, euros, and pounds.

This knowledge graph describes additional attributes of catalog contents in a product/catalog management domain. Its primary entities are catalog content attribute records linked to catalog entries, with key properties such as attribute identifier, attribute value, catalog entry identifier, catalog level number, and references to related catalog entries and their levels.

A knowledge graph of catalog structures and hierarchical catalog entries, representing positions within a catalog hierarchy. Each catalog entry is described by attributes such as a catalog identifier, level name, level number, a reference to another catalog id (e.g., a parent or linked entry), and its type/classification.

A metadata knowledge graph of attribute definitions describing data elements used in a system. Each attribute-definition entity is characterized by key properties such as an attribute identifier, an attribute name, an attribute data type, and classification/type information suitable for filtering or selection.

This knowledge graph contains metadata about catalogs, with catalog records as the primary entities; each record includes attributes such as catalog identifier, catalog name, publisher, date of publication, and date of latest revision.

A knowledge graph of discount coupons representing individual coupon records and their properties. Key entities are coupons, described by attributes such as coupon identifier, discount amount, and date issued for filtering or selection.

This knowledge graph describes payment transactions for customer bookings, modeling payment records linked to customers and bookings. Each payment entity includes attributes such as payment ID, booking ID, customer ID, payment date, amount due, amount paid, a flag indicating paid-in-full, and payment type code.

This knowledge graph models bookings and hire/rental transactions, focusing on booking records and their associated customers. Each booking record includes identifiers and dates (booking ID, start and end), status and counts (status code, number hired, returned-damaged flag), and financial attributes (amount payable, amount outstanding, amount of refund, amount of discount) along with customer identifiers.

This knowledge graph describes products available for hire, representing individual rentable items and their classifications. Each product is characterized by identifiers, names, textual descriptions, product type codes, and daily hire cost — attributes commonly used for filtering, selection, and pricing queries.

This KG describes customer records for a business, representing individual customers and their associated coupons. Each customer entity includes identifiers and personal attributes (customer ID, first and last name, gender), coupon IDs or references, timestamps (date they became a customer and date of last hire/activity), and a label indicating whether the customer is considered good or bad.

This KG describes product booking records, linking bookings and products and representing items reserved or purchased within booking transactions. Each record includes attributes such as booking ID and product ID (and reference IDs), booked amount and booked count, and boolean flags for returned and returned-late status.

This knowledge graph describes product availability information, linking products and their associated bookings. Key entities are products, bookings, and availability records, with important attributes including an availability flag (available yes/no), booking ID, product ID, reference booking/product IDs, and a status date.

This knowledge graph describes retail products, with primary entities representing individual product items. Each product is characterized by identifiers and labels (product ID, name, description), classification and color codes (and references to those codes), and pricing attributes (typical buying price and typical selling price).

This knowledge graph models product characteristics and their values within a product/catalog domain. Its primary entities are product-characteristic association records that link products (product_id and optional referenced product_id) to characteristics (characteristic_id and optional referenced characteristic_id) and record the corresponding characteristic value.

This knowledge graph describes characteristic definitions used to annotate entities in a domain, with the main entities representing individual characteristics. Key attributes include a characteristic identifier, name, data type, type code, and references to characteristic type codes.

The knowledge graph catalogs reference colors and their classifications. Main entities are individual color entries, with key attributes including a color code, a textual color description, and a type or category for each color.

This knowledge graph contains reference records for characteristic types used to classify attributes or features within a larger data model. Each characteristic type entity includes a unique code, a human-readable description, and its type/class affiliation.

This knowledge graph contains reference data about product categories, representing individual product category records. Each record includes attributes such as product category code, a human-readable description, unit of measure, and category/type classification.

This knowledge graph describes broadcast audience share data, representing records that link channels and programs to measured shares. Key entities are broadcast-share records, channels, and programs; important attributes include channel ID, program ID, reference channel/program IDs, broadcast date, and share (percentage).

This knowledge graph describes programs (organizational initiatives or projects) as the primary domain, representing each program entity with associated metadata. Key attributes captured for each program include its name, launch date, origin, owning organization, and a unique program identifier.

A knowledge graph about broadcast scheduling and airings, representing broadcast instances that link channels and programs. Key entities include broadcasts, channels, and programs, with important attributes for channel identifier, program identifier, referenced channel/program identifiers, and the time of day of the broadcast.

Knowledge graph describing channels (e.g., media or distribution/marketing channels) as the primary entities. Each channel is characterized by an identifier, a name, an owner, a rating percentage, and a share percentage.

This knowledge graph contains information about buildings as individual entities. For each building it records key identifying and physical attributes such as an internal identifier, name, street address, number of floors, height (in feet), and years it held the status of tallest.

A knowledge graph describing educational institutions (e.g., schools, colleges, universities) and related entities such as teams and campus buildings. Key attributes include institution identifiers and names, location, founding date, enrollment, institution type, primary athletic conference, and building identifiers.

This knowledge graph describes protein entities and their related metadata. Key attributes include accession numbers, protein names and common (common) names, sequence length and sequence identity to human proteins, divergence from the human lineage, and institution or reference institution identifiers.

This knowledge graph describes tracks—venues used for racing or events—with entities representing individual track locations. Each track has attributes such as name, geographic location, seating capacity, a unique track identifier, and the year it opened.

Dataset describing race events and their associated race tracks. Each race entity includes attributes such as its name, date, class/category, a unique race identifier, and links to a track identifier or reference to the hosting track.

This knowledge graph models railway management relationships, representing records that link managers to specific railways and record when management began. Key entities are managers, railways, and the management records that connect them, with primary attributes including manager identifier, railway identifier, the start year of management (from_year), and references to the manager and railway records.

A knowledge graph about trains and railway services describing individual train instances. Each train record includes attributes such as origin station, arrival time, train name, and multiple identifiers (railway identifier, reference railway identifier, train identifier, and train number).

This knowledge graph covers railway assets and related artifacts, modeling individual railway items (such as locomotives or rolling stock) and their affiliations. Key attributes include builder/manufacturer, year built, location, object number and identifiers, railway affiliation, and wheel count.

This knowledge graph describes managers in an organization, representing individual manager entities. Each manager is characterized by attributes such as name, manager ID, age, country, management level, and the year they started working.

A knowledge graph of real estate properties and transactions, representing property listings and sales. Each property entity includes attributes such as agreed selling price, buyer-offered price, vendor-requested price, date on market and date sold, address/ID/name, property type and room count, and apartment features.

This knowledge graph describes real estate property features, representing associations between properties and their individual features. Each record links a property and a feature and provides identifiers for the property and feature, a textual description of the property feature, and optional reference identifiers for the feature and property.

A catalog of reference property types where each entity represents a distinct property type used for classification. Key attributes available for filtering or selection include a property type code, a textual description, and type/classification metadata.

Knowledge graph describing available features/options in a product or offerings catalog. Main entities are feature items with key attributes including a feature identifier, feature name, textual description, feature type code, and a reference to the feature type (used for filtering and selection).

This knowledge graph is a registry of reference feature types used to classify data features and attributes. Its primary entities are feature-type records, each described by key attributes such as a feature type code, a human-readable feature type name, and their type/class classification.

This knowledge graph describes clubs and related organizational entities. Each club is represented with attributes such as a unique identifier, the club name, its region, its start (founding) year, and its classification/type.

A knowledge graph of competition match results for clubs/teams, where the main entities are match-result records tied to clubs and referenced opponent clubs. Key attributes include club identifiers and referenced club identifiers, medal counts (gold, big silver, small silver, bronze), points, and rank.

A knowledge graph of players (individuals/participants) capturing personal, professional, and competitive information. Key attributes include player identifiers and names, gender, occupation, rank, residence, sponsor name, and vote counts.

This knowledge graph describes coaches and their affiliations within sports clubs; the primary entities are coaches (and referenced clubs). Key attributes available for filtering or selection include coach identifiers, coach names, gender, rank, and club affiliation identifiers.

This knowledge graph describes player–coach relationships in a sports context, modeling associations between individual players and their coaches. Each relationship entity records the player and coach identifiers, optional reference identifiers linking to external records, and the starting year of the player–coach relationship.

A knowledge graph of film cast relationships linking actors to films; the primary entities are actor–film association records and the referenced actor and film entities. Each record carries attributes such as actor ID, film ID, reference IDs for the actor and film, and a last-update timestamp.

This knowledge graph contains country-related data, with entities representing countries and key attributes including the country name, a country identifier, a last-update timestamp, and type/classification metadata.

This knowledge graph describes payment transactions (payments for a rental system), with payment records as the central entities. Key attributes include payment ID, amount, payment date, customer and rental references (customer_id, rental_id), staff ID, and last-update timestamps.

This knowledge graph describes customer records in a retail/service context, representing individual customers and their account metadata. Each customer entity includes identifiers (customer_id, address_id, store_id, ref-address_id), personal details (first_name, last_name, email), status flags (active), and timestamps (create_date, last_update).

This KG models retail inventory records for films, representing inventory items that link specific films to store locations. Each inventory record includes attributes such as inventory identifier, film identifier (and reference film id), store identifier, and last-update timestamp.

This knowledge graph describes categorical classifications within a dataset, where the primary entities are categories and each category is characterized by attributes such as a unique identifier, a human-readable name, a last-update timestamp, and a type/classification label.

This knowledge graph describes film categorization, representing records that link films to their assigned categories. Each film-category record includes key attributes such as film and category identifiers, reference identifiers for those IDs, and a last-update timestamp.

This knowledge graph describes rental transactions in a rental business, representing rental records and their links to customers, inventory items, and staff. Each rental record includes identifiers (rental, customer, inventory), rental and return dates, the staff handling the transaction, and metadata such as last update and reference links to customer and inventory.

This knowledge graph describes cities and related geographical/administrative information. Each city entity includes attributes such as the city name, a unique city identifier, an associated country identifier (and reference to the country), and a last-update timestamp.

This knowledge graph describes actors (persons) and their records. Each actor entity includes key attributes such as a unique actor identifier, first name, last name, a last-update timestamp, and type/class information.

Knowledge graph of films/movies describing individual film records. Each film entity includes identifiers and metadata such as title and description, release year, language, duration (length), rating, rental duration and rate, replacement cost, special features, and last-update timestamps.

This knowledge graph represents address and location records, capturing postal and contact information for places or entities. Each address entity includes attributes such as street and secondary address lines, unique address identifiers, city identifiers or references, district, postal code, phone number, and last-update timestamps.

This knowledge graph covers school transportation records, describing school buses and their relationships to drivers and schools. For each bus it captures key attributes such as driver identifiers and references, school identifiers/references, whether the driver is full‑time, and the driver’s years of working.

This knowledge graph describes educational institutions (schools) and their metadata. Each school entity is characterized by attributes such as grades served, geographic location, a school name/label, a unique school identifier, and the school's type or category.

This knowledge graph describes drivers (individual people) and their associated identifying and demographic information. For each driver it records attributes such as name, driver identifier, age, home city, and party affiliation.

This knowledge graph describes schools and their institutional and athletic attributes. Each school entity includes identifiers and names plus attributes such as county, geographic location, enrollment, mascot, and athletic classifications (overall IHSAA class and IHSAA football class).

A knowledge graph of school budget records, representing yearly financial allocations and expenditures for individual schools. Each record includes school identifiers and year plus key attributes such as amount budgeted, amount invested, percent of budget invested, and overall percent of total budget budgeted/invested.

This knowledge graph describes endowment and donation records associated with educational institutions. Key entities are individual endowment entries and schools, with attributes such as donation amount, donor name, endowment identifier, school identifier, and referenced school identifier.

This knowledge graph describes individual players and their roster/biographical details. Key entities are player records with attributes such as player identifier, player name, age, playing position, team affiliation, school identifier, and references to school records.

This knowledge graph describes educational institutions (schools) and their associated metadata. Key entities are individual schools with attributes such as enrollment, founding year, location, religious denomination, gender composition (boys/girls/coed), day vs. boarding status, school colors, unique identifiers, and year entered competition.

This knowledge graph describes school performance records, with entities representing schools and their per-year performance entries. Key attributes include performance classifications (class A, class AA), school identifiers (school id and reference school id), and the school year.

A knowledge graph of schools and their organizational/athletic details. It contains individual school records with attributes such as class (classification), team colors, division, league, nickname, and identifiers (school_id and reference id) that can be used to filter or select schools.

This knowledge graph describes projects and their metadata, with each project entity represented along with key attributes such as a project code (identifier), project name, logged or allocated hours, and its classification/type.

This KG describes assignment records linking scientists to research projects. Key entities are assignments, scientists, and projects, with important attributes including the associated project, the associated scientist, and reference identifiers used to cross-reference the project and scientist.

A knowledge graph about scientists, representing individual scientists (people) as the primary entities. Key attributes include personal name, social security number (SSN), and type/class membership used to categorize or filter those scientist entities.

Contains information about ship captains and their roles in a maritime context. Key entities are captains and their associated vessels, with attributes such as name, age, rank, captain identifier, vessel/ship identifiers (including referenced ship IDs) and vessel class.

A knowledge graph of maritime vessels where each entity represents an individual ship, described by attributes such as name, unique ship identifier, vessel type and class, flag/state of registration, and year built. These key attributes are typically used for filtering, identification, and retrieval of ship records.

This knowledge graph describes missions and their associated ships, focusing on maritime or vessel operations. Each mission entity includes attributes such as mission code and identifier, associated ship identifiers, launch year, location, speed in knots, and mission fate/outcome.

This knowledge graph covers maritime vessels, representing individual ships as the primary entities. Each ship is described by attributes commonly used for identification and classification, including name, nationality (flag), unique ship identifier, tonnage, and vessel type.

This knowledge graph contains records of members in a membership/loyalty system, with each entity representing an individual member or account. Key attributes available for filtering or selection include member identifier, name, card number, membership level, and hometown.

This knowledge graph describes branch membership records for an organization, representing entries that link individual members to specific branches. Each membership entry includes attributes such as branch identifier, member identifier, corresponding reference identifiers, and the register year, which are commonly used to filter or select records.

This knowledge graph describes branches/locations of an organization (e.g., company or bank branches), with each branch represented as an entity. Key attributes include branch identifier, name, street address, city, opening year, and membership amount (a membership-related metric).

This knowledge graph represents purchase transactions, with each transaction record linked to branch and member identifiers (including referenced branch/member IDs), a total quantity in pounds, and the year of the purchase.

This knowledge graph contains information about singers (individual musical artists), with each singer described by attributes such as name, birth year, citizenship, net worth (in millions), and an internal singer identifier. It is suitable for querying or filtering singers by demographics (e.g., birth year, citizenship), identity (name or ID), and economic measures (net worth).

A knowledge graph of songs and their metadata. It describes song entities with attributes such as title and identifiers (song ID, singer ID, reference/featured singer ID), commercial metrics (sales), and chart performance (highest chart position).

Knowledge graph about accounts and account holders, where the primary entities are account records (customers/accounts). Key attributes available for selection or filtering include customer identifier (ID), the account or person name, and an entity type/classification.

This knowledge graph models savings account records and their relationships to customers, representing individual savings accounts and associated customer entities. Key attributes include account balance, customer identifier, reference customer identifier, and entity type/class information.

This knowledge graph models checking (bank) accounts and their connections to customers, with main entities representing individual checking accounts. Key attributes include account balance, customer identifier, and referenced customer identifier, and entities are labeled by type.
A knowledge graph of countries, representing country entities with attributes such as identifier values, country names, and classification/type information.

This knowledge graph describes football (soccer) teams as entities, capturing identifiers and naming information. Key attributes available for queries include internal IDs, external API identifiers (including FIFA IDs), long and short team names, and type/classification metadata.

Knowledge graph about soccer (football) player attribute records; each entity represents a player’s attribute snapshot (often dated) linked to a player identifier. A knowledge graph about soccer/football teams and their tactical/performance attribute records. Key entities are teams and per-team attribute entries, with attributes including buildup-play metrics (dribbling, passing, speed, positioning and their qualitative classes), chance-creation metrics (crossing, passing, shooting, positioning and classes), defensive metrics (aggression, pressure, defender line, team width and classes), plus identifiers and date fields.

This knowledge graph describes football (soccer) players and their associated data. It represents player entities with identifiers (id, player_api_id, player_fifa_api_id), personal attributes (player_name, birthday) and physical attributes commonly queried such as height and weight.

Knowledge graph about sports leagues, representing league entities and their metadata. Each league is described by attributes such as a unique identifier, a human-readable name, a country identifier and references to country records, plus type/classification information.

A knowledge graph about individual sports players (athletes), representing each player as an entity. Key attributes include player identifiers and names, performance/statistic fields (e.g., "hs"), disciplinary data such as yellow-card counts ("ycard"), and class/type annotations.

This knowledge graph represents records of entities involved in decision-making or application processes (such as candidates, persons, or organizations). Each record includes attributes commonly used for identification and review: a canonical name, a decision outcome, a person or process identifier, a position or role, and reference names/identifiers.

This knowledge graph describes colleges and related institutional information. It contains entities representing colleges with key attributes such as college name, enrollment (student numbers), state (location), and type/classification.

A knowledge graph of financial records and finance-related items. Each finance entity (e.g., a transaction or finance record) is described by a finance identifier, additional descriptive details, and a type/classification attribute.

This knowledge graph describes associations between products and events, capturing which products are involved in or linked to particular events; the primary entities are products, events, and the product-in-event association records.
