This knowledge graph describes occurrences of assets in events, modeling which assets are associated with which events. Key entities are asset-event records linking individual assets to events, with primary attributes including asset identifiers, event identifiers, optional reference-event identifiers, and type/classification of the record.

A knowledge graph of address records describing physical/postal addresses. Each address entity includes a unique identifier, structured address details (e.g., street, city, postal code) and a type/classification attribute.

A knowledge graph of event records where each event entity is described by identifiers and metadata including an event ID, event type code, communication channel, and linked finance, location, and address information (with reference identifiers). Typical attributes used for filtering or selection are event ID, event type, channel, finance references, location references, and address identifiers.

A knowledge graph about agreements and their associated events, representing agreement records/documents and event instances. Each agreement is described by attributes such as a document identifier, an event identifier, references to related events, and its classification/type.

A knowledge graph of locations where the primary entities are location records. Each location is described by a unique location identifier, additional descriptive details, and a type/classification attribute.

This knowledge graph captures relationships between parties and events, documenting which parties participate in which events. Key entities are events and parties, with important attributes including event identifiers, party identifiers, reference identifiers linking to external records, and role codes specifying each party's role in the event.

A knowledge graph about products, describing individual product items as the primary entities. Each product is characterized by key attributes such as a product identifier, product name, product price, product type code, and classification labels.

Knowledge graph describing channels (e.g., communication or distribution channels), where the main entities are individual channel records and the key attributes include a channel identifier, miscellaneous/other details about each channel, and a type/classification for each channel.

This knowledge graph describes parties (entities such as organizations or participants), with each party represented by a unique identifier, descriptive details about the party, and classification/type information.

This knowledge graph describes assets and their metadata, focusing on individual asset entities. Key attributes include a unique asset identifier, descriptive or other details, and classification/type information for each asset.

Knowledge graph about team sports players, describing individual athletes, their club affiliations, and performance statistics. Each player entity is characterized by attributes such as name and player identifier, club membership, position, appearances (apps), goals, tries, and points.

This knowledge graph describes competition results for events, where each result record links two clubs and a competition. Key entities are result entries, clubs, and competitions, and important attributes include the identifiers for club 1 and club 2, the competition identifier, the match score, and references linking results to the corresponding club and competition records.

This knowledge graph describes clubs (organizational entities), with each club represented by key attributes such as a unique identifier, name, region/location, founding/start year, and classification/type. A knowledge graph about competitions, where the primary entities are individual competition events described by attributes such as a competition identifier, competition type, host country, and year, together with their class/type information.

This knowledge graph contains club ranking and performance data, describing clubs (or club ranking records) and their standings in competitions. Key attributes include club identifiers (and reference identifiers), rank/position, counts of gold, silver, and bronze (and total) medals or points.

A knowledge graph of railway routes, describing route records that associate trains with stations. Key entities are routes, trains, and stations, with important attributes including train identifiers, station identifiers, and reference fields that link each route to a specific train and station.

This knowledge graph contains weekly weather observations represented as individual daily records for monitoring stations. Each record includes attributes such as day of week, high and low temperatures, precipitation amount, wind speed (mph), and station identifiers (station id and reference station id).

This knowledge graph describes train services and schedules, representing individual trains as the primary entities. Key attributes include origin and destination stations, departure time, train number and name, a unique identifier, and service interval (frequency), which are the main fields used for filtering or selecting records.

This knowledge graph describes transportation stations as entities and their key attributes, including unique identifiers, the responsible local authority, network affiliation (network name), services offered, and classification/type information.

A knowledge graph of product offerings, primarily printing and imaging devices. Each product entity is described by attributes such as physical dimensions, resolution (dpi), interface type, maximum page size, color pages-per-minute performance, and product identifiers.

This knowledge graph describes store-product records linking products to the stores that carry them. Its primary entities are store-product association records, with key attributes including product identifiers, store identifiers, and reference identifiers that link to external product or store records.

This knowledge graph describes administrative districts and their associated cities, representing each district with key attributes such as a district identifier and name, the city where it is headquartered, and city-level metrics like population and area.

A knowledge graph of retail stores, representing individual store entities. Each store includes attributes useful for querying and filtering such as store identifier and name, store type, area size, number of product categories, and ranking (performance).

A knowledge graph of store-to-district associations in a retail/location-management domain, containing entities that represent store-district association records. Key attributes available for filtering or selection include store identifiers, district identifiers, and reference identifiers linking to stores or districts.

This knowledge graph models regions impacted by storms, representing affected-region entities and their associations to storm events and geographic regions. Key attributes include the number of cities affected and identifiers/references that link each affected region to a region record and to a storm event.

This knowledge graph describes storms and individual storm events, representing each storm as a distinct entity with a name and identifier. For each storm it records key attributes useful for filtering or analysis such as active dates, maximum wind speed, estimated damage (in millions of USD), and number of deaths.

The knowledge graph describes geographical or administrative regions; its primary entities are region records. Each region is characterized by attributes such as a region identifier, a region code, a region name, and a classification/type, which are commonly used for selection or filtering.

A knowledge graph representing a roster of individuals (e.g., students or listed persons) in an educational or group context. Key entities are the list entries for people, described by attributes such as first name, last name, classroom assignment, grade, and entity type.

A knowledge graph about teachers in an educational context, representing individual teacher entities. Key attributes include first name, last name, classroom assignment, and the teacher's classification/type within the system.

This knowledge graph contains records of candidate assessments, representing assessment events for individuals in a recruitment or educational context. This knowledge graph describes people (individuals) and their personal and account-related information; key attributes include identifiers (person ID, login name), names (first, middle, last), contact details (email address, cell/mobile number), and authentication data (password).

This knowledge graph describes educational courses as the primary entities. Each course record includes key attributes such as a unique course identifier, a course name, a textual course description, and its classification/type.

This knowledge graph contains records of physical mailing addresses. Each address entity includes an identifier and key attributes such as street lines (line 1 and line 2), city, state/province/county, postal/ZIP code, and country.

Knowledge graph about student course attendance, representing attendance records that link students with courses. Each attendance record includes attributes such as student identifier, course identifier (including a combined student-course reference) and the date of attendance.

This knowledge graph models academic student course registrations, representing enrollment records that link students and courses. Each registration record includes attributes such as student identifier, course identifier, reference links to the student and course entities, and the registration date.

A knowledge graph of people and their address records, modeling links between individuals and physical addresses. Each record includes identifiers for the person and the address (and a unique person-address record id), temporal attributes for the residency period (start and end dates), and reference identifiers.

A knowledge graph about candidates, representing individual candidate entities (e.g., for elections, appointments, or applications). Each candidate record includes attributes such as a candidate identifier, a reference candidate identifier, descriptive candidate details, and type/classification metadata.

A knowledge graph describing students and their records. Its primary entities are individual student profiles, with key attributes including student identifiers (primary and reference IDs), student details (personal or academic information), and class/type membership.

This knowledge graph describes organizational departments within an institution or company. Each department entity is represented by key attributes such as a unique identifier, a human-readable name, a textual description, and its type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes postal address records as its primary entities. Each address is characterized by a unique identifier and typical address attributes such as street lines (line 1 and line 2), city, state/province/county, ZIP/postcode, and country.

This knowledge graph describes academic course sections in an educational context. Each section entity includes identifiers (section_id, course_id, ref-course_id), a section name, and a section description that are the primary attributes for filtering or selection.

This knowledge graph represents courses (academic or training offerings) as the primary entities, with key attributes including course identifier, course name, and course description. Each course is also associated with a classification/type attribute for grouping or filtering by category.

This knowledge graph describes academic degree programs offered by an institution, modeling each program and its relationship to departments. Key entities are degree program records and departments, with important attributes including program identifiers, program names, summary descriptions, department identifiers, and links referencing the associated department.

This knowledge graph represents student records for an educational institution, modeling individual students and their identifying, contact, and enrollment information. Knowledge graph about student enrollments in academic courses, representing association records that link individual student enrollment instances to course offerings. Key entities are enrollment-course association records, student enrollments, and courses; important attributes include course identifiers, student enrollment identifiers, association (student-course) identifiers, and reference IDs that link enrollments to courses.

A knowledge graph about student enrollment records that represent links between individual students, degree programs, and academic semesters. A knowledge graph of transcript records describing individual transcript documents or entries. Each transcript entity includes key attributes such as a unique transcript identifier, the transcript date, and its type/classification.

This knowledge graph models academic transcript content, where the primary entities are transcript content records that link individual student-course enrollments to specific transcripts. Each record includes key attributes such as a transcript identifier, a student-course identifier, and reference IDs that connect the entry to the corresponding transcript and student-course records.

This knowledge graph describes academic semesters as the primary entities. Each semester is represented with key attributes such as a unique identifier, a name, a descriptive summary, and classification/type information.

A knowledge graph about competitive swimmers, where the primary entities are individual swimmers (athletes) and their performance records. Key attributes include an identifier, name, nationality, split times at 100m, 200m, 300m, 400m, 500m, 600m and 700m distances, and overall time.

This knowledge graph describes events and their relationships to venues, representing event entities with key attributes such as unique identifiers, names, associated stadium/venue identifiers or references, and the year of the event. This knowledge graph describes stadiums (sports venues) and related place entities. Each stadium is characterized by attributes such as name and identifier, seating capacity, city and country location, and opening (year).

This knowledge graph contains competitive swimming competition records, modeling individual race results and their associated events and athletes. Each record entity captures identifiers and references to the swimmer and event plus the performance result (e.g., time or placement).
A knowledge graph describing artists and their records. Each artist entity includes key attributes such as name, unique artist identifier, age, country, and the year they joined.

Knowledge graph of exhibition records describing individual exhibitions or entries for exhibition events. Each record includes attributes such as attendance figures, date, exhibition identifiers and reference identifiers, and type/classification metadata useful for filtering, grouping, and identification.

A knowledge graph about art and cultural exhibitions, describing exhibitions and their associated artists. Key entities are exhibitions and artist records, with attributes including exhibition ID, artist ID (and reference artist ID), theme, ticket price, and year.

A knowledge graph of project task records: each task entity represents a work item associated with a project and includes identifiers, descriptive details, and type/classification metadata. A knowledge graph describing projects and their relationships to organisations. Key entities are projects and organisations, with attributes such as project identifier, project details, organisation identifier/reference, and entity type classification.

This knowledge graph describes research staff and their affiliations with organizations; each staff entity represents a researcher or staff member and includes identifiers (staff ID, employer organisation ID and reference employer organisation ID), descriptive staff details, and classification/type metadata.

This knowledge graph contains records of documents related to grant administration, representing document entities and their links to grants. This knowledge graph describes project staffing and staff assignments, modeling which staff members are assigned to which projects. This knowledge graph describes organisation types, with individual entries representing different categories of organisations. Key attributes include the organisation type name, a textual description of the organisation type, and categorical classification labels for each entry.

This knowledge graph models staff roles within an organization, with each role represented as an entity. Key attributes for these role entities include a role code, a role description, and a classification/type used for filtering or selection.

This knowledge graph describes grant awards and associated organisations, representing individual grants and the organisations involved. Key attributes include grant identifiers, funding amounts, grant start and end dates, organisation identifiers (and references), and other descriptive details for filtering or selecting grants.

This knowledge graph contains information about organisations and their metadata. Key entities are organisation records, with important attributes including organisation identifiers, descriptive details, organisation type/classification, and references to type authority or taxonomy.

This knowledge graph covers project outcomes, representing outcome records that associate projects with standardized outcome codes. Main entities are project outcome entries and projects, with key attributes including project identifier, outcome code, and reference identifiers linking to canonical project and outcome records.

This knowledge graph models document types in a document-management/domain taxonomy, where each entity represents a specific document-type entry. Key attributes available for selection and filtering are a human-readable document description, a standardized document type code, and a categorical classification (type).

This knowledge graph contains records of research outcomes, representing individual outcome entries from research projects or studies. Each outcome entity is described by attributes such as an outcome code, a textual outcome description, and a classification/type label.

This knowledge graph describes shipment items in the shipping and order-fulfillment domain. Each shipment-item entity includes identifiers and links such as order item ID, shipment ID, reference order-item ID, reference shipment ID, and type metadata, which are the primary attributes for filtering and selection.

This knowledge graph describes order line items in an e-commerce/order-management domain, representing individual items associated with customer orders and products. Each order item includes identifiers (order item ID, order ID, product ID), an item status, and links to the referenced order and product.

This knowledge graph contains retail and transactional order records, with individual orders as the primary entities. Each order is described by key attributes such as order identifier, customer identifier (including a customer reference), order placement date, and order status, which are commonly used for filtering and retrieval.

A knowledge graph describing products in a product catalog, where the primary entities are individual product items. Each product is characterized by attributes such as a product identifier, a product name, and a type/classification, which are commonly used for filtering or selecting products.

A knowledge graph of customer data for an organization, where the primary entities are individual customers. Each customer is described by key attributes such as customer ID, customer name, detailed customer information, and type/class labels.

A knowledge graph of shipment and logistics records where the primary entities are individual shipments. Each shipment is described by attributes such as shipment ID, shipment tracking number, shipment date, invoice number and reference invoice number, and order ID and reference order ID.

This knowledge graph covers the invoicing/billing domain and represents individual invoice records as the primary entities. Each invoice includes key attributes such as invoice number, invoice date, invoice details, and its classification/type.

This knowledge graph describes purchase transactions and related purchase records. Each purchase entity includes attributes such as a transaction identifier, a reference transaction identifier, descriptive purchase details, and a classification/type.

This knowledge graph models records of lots and their associations with transactions. Key entities are lot and transaction records, with important attributes including lot identifier, transaction identifier, reference lot identifier, reference transaction identifier, and a type/classification attribute.

This knowledge graph describes lots (e.g., auction or investment lots) and their relationships to investors, representing entities for lots and investor references. Key attributes include lot identifiers, lot details or descriptions, investor identifiers and reference investor identifiers, and type/class labels used to categorize each record.

This knowledge graph covers sales transactions, representing individual sales records as the primary entities. Each record includes key attributes such as a transaction identifier and reference identifier, descriptive sales details, and type/classification metadata.

The KG contains reference data about transaction types used in financial and valuation processes; its primary entities are transaction-type records. Each record includes a transaction type code, a human-readable description, and a classification/type label.

This knowledge graph describes financial transaction records (primarily investor securities transactions) and linked investor entities. Each transaction is characterized by attributes such as transaction ID, investor identifier (and referenced investor), transaction type code, date of transaction, amount of transaction, and share count.

A knowledge graph about investors, where the primary entities are individual investor records. Each investor is described by key attributes such as a unique investor identifier, descriptive investor details (e.g., profile or metadata), and type/class annotations indicating investor categories.

This knowledge graph describes television series broadcasts and episodes, recording individual TV program entries. Each entry includes attributes such as air date, broadcast channel (and referenced channel), episode and unique identifiers, and audience metrics including rating, rating share, share, viewers (millions), and weekly rank.

This knowledge graph describes television channels and their metadata, modeling channel entities and their associated attributes. Key attributes include programming/content, country of origin, language, unique channel identifier, high-definition availability, package options and pay-per-view status, pixel aspect ratio, and series names—fields commonly used to filter or select channels.

A knowledge graph of cartoon television entries, where each entity represents a cartoon episode or work. Key attributes available for filtering or selection include title, unique identifier, original air date, production/production code, broadcast channel (and channel reference), director, and writer.

This knowledge graph represents social media posts (tweets) and their associated metadata. Each post entity includes attributes such as text content, creation date, a unique identifier, the author/user identifier, and any referenced-user identifier.

This knowledge graph models user profiles in a social/identity domain, with the main entities being individual user accounts. Key attributes include display names, email addresses, unique identifiers (UIDs), follower relationships (followers), and partition identifiers for grouping or sharding.

This KG models "follow" relationships between entities (e.g., accounts or agents) in a network. Its primary entities are follow records that link two parties, with attributes for the two related parties (e.g., follower and followee), additional reference identifiers or reference fields, and type/class metadata for each record.

This knowledge graph encodes mappings between telephone area codes and the states or regions they cover. Its primary entities are area-code-to-state mapping records, with key attributes for the area code value and the associated state/region (used for filtering or selection).

This knowledge graph describes contestants in a competition, where the primary entities are individual contestants and their classifications; key attributes include each contestant’s name and contestant number.

A knowledge graph of voting records (e.g., phone-in or recorded votes). Each vote entity is described by attributes such as vote identifier, phone number and area code (and referenced area code), contestant number (and referenced contestant), creation timestamp, and vote state.

This knowledge graph describes people (individual persons) as its primary entities, with key attributes used for selection or filtering including a unique person identifier, name, age, gender, and country of residence.

This knowledge graph describes churches as entities and their institutional relationships. For each church it provides key attributes such as a unique identifier, the church name, opening/establishment date, who organized or founded it, and links to predecessor or continuation churches.

Knowledge graph of wedding records: it models wedding events linking participants (male and female persons) and church venues. Each wedding record includes key attributes such as male and female identifiers, church identifier, reference identifiers for those entities, and the year of the wedding.

A knowledge graph about workshops/events, with entities representing individual workshops; key attributes include the workshop name, date, venue, a unique workshop identifier, and the workshop type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes acceptance records for workshop submissions, linking individual submissions to workshops and recording the acceptance outcome. Key entities are acceptance entries, submissions, and workshops, with important attributes including submission identifiers, workshop identifiers, reference identifiers linking submissions and workshops, and the acceptance result/decision.

This knowledge graph contains records of submissions (e.g., academic or competition entries), with each submission as a central entity. Key attributes available for querying and filtering include the submission's author, affiliated college, numeric scores, a submission identifier, and its type/classification.

This knowledge graph describes cities and related geographic information: each city entity is represented with attributes such as a unique identifier, name, population, district, country code, and a reference to its country. It is suited for queries that filter or select cities by name, population, district, or country affiliation.

This knowledge graph contains country-level information describing sovereign states and territories. Each country entity is annotated with attributes such as capital city, country codes, continent and region, population and surface area, GNP (and historical GNP), government form and head of state, independence year, life expectancy, and local and common names.

This knowledge graph describes languages spoken in countries, with entities representing country-language relationships linking a country to a specific language. Key attributes include the country identifier, the language name, whether the language is official, the percentage of speakers, and a reference country code.

This knowledge graph describes professional wrestlers and their championship reigns, including individual wrestlers, title reigns, events, and event locations. Key attributes include wrestler names and IDs, reign identifiers or numbers, duration of reigns (days held), and associated event and location details.

This knowledge graph models elimination events in wrestling matches, with primary entities for elimination records, wrestlers, and teams. Each elimination record includes attributes such as the eliminated wrestler and who eliminated them, the elimination move, time, an elimination identifier, and references to wrestler IDs and teams.
